gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Braid is round woven strands. Braid now builds round strands that twist over and under each other, with Spread to pack or open the weave; plus a start-up splash that works on Wayland. How it works

Added
  • Palm rejection (Android): fingers that land while the pen is in range, or in the 0.3 s after it leaves, are a resting palm and do nothing; a trackpad's fingers are never ignored. Off on desktop touch screens.
  • Android (early, members first; free for everyone on 26 November): SculptForge builds for Android tablets, phones and Chromebooks (arm64 and x86_64, Android 9 or later, OpenGL ES 3.2) as a sideloaded APK. Sculpt with a finger or a stylus with pressure, navigate with two fingers (pan, pinch to zoom, twist to roll), undo, save to the app's Projects folder and open any file through the system's document picker. The desktop layout for now; a tablet layout of its own comes next (android/README.md).
  • Palm rejection (Android): fingers that land while the pen is in range, or in the 0.3 s after it leaves, are a resting palm and do nothing; a trackpad's fingers are never ignored. A pen that never reports leaving stops counting after 3 s. Off on desktop touch screens; Preferences > Tablet > Ignore fingers while the pen is near turns it on or off.
Changed
  • Braid (Tool > Tube) now builds round strands (two to begin with) that twist over and under each other round the curve, instead of flat ribbons. Spread sets the weave: 0 packs the strands together so they touch, 1 opens them up with longer turns. Saved braids look different. Requested by Artizmo on Discord.
  • Release tooling: the members' beta is created in the insiders repository with its own tag target, so a beta no longer stops at "tag has not been pushed".
  • Why page: the agents are described as testing for speed, stability and feel, with artists deciding what gets built.
  • Guide: the install page now says Android is in early access for members, public on 26 November, instead of "no Android version".
  • The start-up splash shows on every interactive start for at least 0.5 s (overlapped with start-up work), centred and floating, and fades into the main window. Turn it off in Preferences > Interface > Show startup splash.
  • Four home-page demo clips and 25 guide screenshots showed old interface labels; the site leaves them out until they are re-recorded on current main.
  • Website home page: a release's news appears once, in the announcement bar under the menu; the hero and the What's new heading no longer repeat it. The release card check (scripts/release.sh) looks for the bar, and a colon-chain tagline fails the guide check.
  • Website: the home page and the About page now show what is built in: Blender round-trip, Gaussian splats with Blender 5.3, capture to sculptable mesh, quad retopology and baking, garments and cloth, and the optional AI brushes. Blender and splats lead in the hero on desktop and phone, with a six-tile "Built in" band below it.
Fixed
  • Nudge and Palette Knife folded the surface over itself (#198, #199): a second stroke across an area they had dragged, and a single Nudge stroke, left thousands of triangles folded over their neighbours (dark creases and specks). The material they push is now spread out again behind the brush; Palette Knife drags a little less per dab when its steps are long (at the default spacing it drags as far as before); Nudge slides along the plane of the brush instead of each vertex's own, noisy normal (which also keeps the two halves of a mirrored stroke identical), and holds back a move that would turn a triangle over while its brush covers up to about 12,000 vertices. In the close-up session the folded triangles fall from 1,444 to 607 (Palette Knife) and Nudge adds none (it added 4,972); on a replay of the same strokes Nudge goes from 5,347 to 0 and Palette Knife from 1,381 to about 620. Palette Knife still leaves creases where two strokes overlap. Cost: Palette Knife takes about 0.2 ms more per dab with a small brush and 40 to 50% more time with a very large one; Nudge about 1.2 ms more per dab with a small brush (the fold check), little more with a large one. Nudge reaches about 6% less far on a long stroke. Tendril is unchanged.
  • The start-up splash never appeared on Wayland ("Window framebuffer support not available"); it is now drawn through an SDL renderer when the window has no surface, and fully drawn before the window is shown.
  • Spikes and streaks from stacked Crease and Inflate strokes (#194): on a divided mesh (about 5 million triangles) Crease packs the triangles across its line, and Inflate, moving every point along its own normal, then flipped them (twenty overlapping strokes left about 2,000 folded triangles and needles). A dab that reaches such a packed grid now swells along the brush's normal instead; Inflate on an ordinary surface is unchanged.
  • Undo history and memory (#202, slice 1; thanks @TheLycanFenrir): the undo history now fits the computer's free memory (a quarter of its total memory, never below 256 MB) instead of a fixed 1 GB that could run an 8 GB computer out of memory next to a very dense mesh, and a 64 GB computer keeps far more history. When steps must go, the status line says "Oldest N undo steps removed to free memory" (English, Spanish and both Chinese) instead of dropping them silently, and Preferences > Performance shows the live budget. Saving older steps to disk and unloading hidden Parts are planned for the rest of #202.

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Mouse orbit speed. Set how fast the mouse turns the view, plus fixes for textured-brush symmetry and Crisp Flatten. How it works

Added
  • Mouse orbit speed in Preferences > Input (thanks hullalmiah on Discord): 0.1x-2x for mouse and trackpad rotation drags in every input style, including orbiting around the pointer; 1x is the turn as it was. The pen keeps its own View speed. Saved in the preferences.
  • Two-key window (Preferences > Input): how long the second key of a two-key shortcut has, 0.35 to 1 s (0.4 s by default). The keys of a two-key shortcut can be pressed together, either one first, or one after the other. A key that is part of one runs its own action once the window is up; every other key runs at once. Update: two-key shortcuts will be removed in the next update; normal shortcuts are not affected.
Changed
  • Release tooling: the Discord release post has a header, the headline first and the release card as its image, with masked Download and What's new links instead of raw URLs.
  • Release tooling: the release stage warns when the version's launch headline is missing, or when its keywords are not in the first highlight line and the What's New tagline; the promote puts the headline first in the GitHub release body, and stages the README's "New in" line.
  • Release tooling: a staging CI run that fails in a test step gets one rerun of its failed jobs, and a test that passes on the rerun is logged as flaky instead of failing the release. A test that fails twice stays red.
Fixed
  • Brush Size and Intensity keep their value when the pointer goes past the canvas edge while you adjust (S / F, U / Shift+F), instead of snapping back to the old one; only a click on another control cancels.
  • Crisp Flatten only cuts down now and never adds clay (thanks Hameron on Discord). Pen pressure no longer scales the Crisp Flatten cut depth (it left terraces across a facet), so a light-pressure stroke lands on the same plane. Surface below the plane is left alone at any depth, which also removes the scattered spikes, debris and stair-steps along the edges of its facets. The regular Flatten brush is still the one that fills dips. The brush's shelf preview is a little wider so the cut shows.
  • Generate 3D (free Hugging Face models): Hunyuan3D 2, 2 mini Turbo and 2.1 and TRELLIS.2 now find their image and prompt inputs by name, so the Spaces adding or reordering inputs (Hunyuan3D now takes 13, TRELLIS.2 15) no longer breaks them. Everything else uses each Space's own defaults.
  • Symmetry with textured brushes (#197): with X or radial symmetry the mirrored strokes of the brushes that stamp a pattern or an alpha (Dragon Scales, Skin Pores, Stone Carve, Wood Grain, Woven Cloth and about 25 more) now carry the pattern's mirror image, where they used to lay a different pattern on each side.

Changed
  • Tests (contributors): a CMakeLists.txt edit that only adds new source files or a guarded add_test runs those files' tests in T0, not the whole suite; the mode matrix runs as four shards side by side; stale_tree runs on every change; a per-push tier (SF_T0_TIER=push: direct picks + start, sculpt, save and open) runs in about half the test time and is never the READY verdict; known flakes go in tests/quarantine.txt with an owner and a date, after which they block again.
Fixed
  • Brush Size and Intensity follow the mouse: press S (or F in the Blender style) or U, move the mouse sideways and the value changes live, with the ring drawn at the live size where you started (Intensity shows a disc inside it). Click or Enter keeps it, Esc or a right click puts it back (thanks hullalmiah on Discord).
  • Undo / Redo of a stroke on a dense model (#181). Every Undo and Redo made the viewport send the whole model to the graphics card again and rebuild its distance-view cache, so the time grew with the model instead of the stroke (5.4M triangles with 3 subdivision levels: 470-600 ms per Ctrl+Z, now 20-30 ms in the frame; the upload itself 500 ms, now 4-8 ms). Only the vertices the stroke changed are sent now. Thanks @TheLycanFenrir and @Devon0209 for the reports.

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.summary: Reference images: your front and side drawings in the view while you sculpt. View > Reference images keeps pictures behind the model or as planes that turn with the view; Front + side... sets up a character's two drawings in one go. Idea by Oslen on Discord.…
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Reference images: your front and side drawings in the view while you sculpt. View > Reference images keeps pictures behind the model or as planes that turn with the view; Front + side... sets up a character's two drawings in one go. Idea by Oslen on Discord. How it works

Added
  • Two-key shortcuts (Preferences > Hotkeys, the >> button beside an action's key): press one key, then a different one within half a second (A then S). Added to the action's other keys; the same key twice is refused; a sequence another action uses asks first (Replace / Cancel); Backspace in that box removes only the two-key shortcuts. A first key that is bound on its own still works: it waits half a second and runs by itself when no second key follows. Requested by Artizmo on Discord.
  • Reference images (View > Reference images; idea by Oslen on Discord): add one or more PNG or JPEG images (or drop them on the window while the section shows). Each sits Behind the model (fixed to the view) or In the scene (a plane at the front, side or top that turns with the view and fades out edge-on), with opacity, flips, lock and hide; Adjust moves it and scales it from its corners (Shift keeps its proportions). Front + side... makes a front and a side plane from two files in one click. They never take strokes or picks and are left out of renders, exports, thumbnails and the timelapse unless Show in renders is on. Projects keep them, embedded or by path; images over 4096 px are scaled down, files over 64 MB, 64 megapixels or 8192 px a side refused (read from the header, before decoding), 8 per project. An image a project names by path opens linked, with Embed off, so saving never copies a file from your computer into it unless you tick Embed. Scriptable: reference_add, reference_set, reference_remove, reference_pair.
Fixed
  • App would not start on some Linux NVIDIA drivers (0.12.5 regression): most likely the start-up splash left its own OpenGL context current, so the main shaders compiled in the wrong context ("Shader compile error" with garbage text, thanks @dCo3lh0 (#192)). The main context is made current again after every splash step, the splash draws a plain software surface, and a start-up shader error now says "no current OpenGL context" or "(empty driver log)" instead of random bytes.
  • A fast mouse or trackpad stroke right after a pen stroke laid only 2 dabs (a mark at each end instead of a line, #195): while the pen is in range the mouse's motion is ignored, because some tablet drivers send stray mouse events beside the pen's, and that also swallowed a stroke the mouse had started. A stroke the mouse began now keeps all of its motion.

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.title: SculptForge v0.12.7
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.summary: Sculpt your scans. Keep them in Blender. Bring a Gaussian splat capture from Blender 5.3 into SculptForge, sculpt against it or turn it into a mesh you can reshape by hand, and send splats back to your scene in one click. Free and open source. How it works…
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Sculpt your scans. Keep them in Blender. Bring a Gaussian splat capture from Blender 5.3 into SculptForge, sculpt against it or turn it into a mesh you can reshape by hand, and send splats back to your scene in one click. Free and open source. How it works

Added
  • "Alpha pool and jitter (Sculpt > Alpha): Scale jitter and Position jitter per dab, kept per brush, and an alpha pool (brush_alpha_pool): a Library folder of images or a few picked alphas, one drawn at random for each dab or Drag Stamp, repeatable per stroke. Three procedural wood-grain alphas (Procedural Wood Straight, Cathedral, Weathered) are named as procedural, not scans. Each stroke now starts its Angle jitter from its own seed, so two strokes no longer jitter identically. Thanks Hameron."
  • Gaussian splats in the Blender bridge (Blender 5.3+, which draws and imports splats but cannot export them): Send to SculptForge sends a selected splat object as a standard 3DGS PLY with its transform; File > Blender > Send to Blender sends the loaded splats back and updates the same object in place. Positions, scales, rotations, opacity and spherical harmonics (up to degree 3) are kept, nothing is baked. The add-on also adds File > Export > Gaussian Splats (.ply) and a drop handler for .splat files; older Blender versions get a message and the mesh bridge is unchanged. The exchange manifest has an optional splats key (older versions skip it). The CI add-on job now also runs bpy 5.3.0.
  • Crisp Flatten brush in the Hard Surface pack (thanks _tfx on Discord): the plane is taken where the stroke starts and held for the whole stroke, and the edge is hard with a thin anti-aliased band (about 2.5 polygons wide), so one stroke cuts one flat facet and two meet in a crisp bevel. It cuts what is above the plane and fills only shallow dips, so it never builds a wall past a curving form. Works with symmetry, masks and Dynamic topology. Brush Lab recipes get Lock plane (off: the plane follows the surface) and Crisp edge, also as planeLock / crispEdge in .sfbrush files and brush_create.
  • Warnings for more destructive operations (#173, thanks @TheLycanFenrir): Delete Masked, Remove Hidden, Split, Mirror, Make Symmetric and Merge by Distance rebuild the mesh and drop the subdivision levels, so on a Part with levels they now ask first, like Voxel Remesh, Quad Remesh and Decimate do (Freeze Levels and Proceed / Cancel). Ctrl+Z still brings the levels back, a Part without levels is not asked, and "Keep original" splits don't ask. Preferences > Interface > Ask before dropping subdivision levels turns the asking off or back on for all of them (and Subdivide).
  • Shift and Ctrl brushes: Shift+click a brush on the bottom shelf (or in the brush picker) to make it the Shift brush, Ctrl+click one on the shelf for the Ctrl brush; the main brush stays. Each keeps its own Intensity, the tile shows a Shift / Ctrl badge and the status line names it. Shift+click Smooth, a mask brush picked with Ctrl held, or Reset Shift brush / Reset Ctrl brush in the command palette go back; Smooth's alternate smooth (#40), Ctrl+Alt unmask, the background mask rectangle and Ctrl+Shift are unchanged. Kept in the preferences; scriptable with set_modifier_brush shift=trim ctrl=flatten. Asked for by Cytrick on Discord.
  • Orbit around the pointer (Edit > Preferences > Input, every key style; on for new installs, off for existing settings so their orbit doesn't change): a rotation drag that starts over the model turns the view about the surface point under the pointer instead of the scene centre, without the view jumping; the target moves to that point's depth, so zooming afterwards works there too (auto depth). Started over the background or on the axis gizmo's disc, it turns about the target as before. Turntable, orbit locks and Shift snapping are kept. The point is picked once per drag (thanks dm4nd on Discord).
  • Booleans between Parts (Tool > Parts): each Part's Boolean (None, Add, Subtract, Intersect) is set from the mark in its row or its right-click menu; the shown Parts with one combine in list order, previewed live in the view (as you sculpt or move them on lighter meshes, on release on heavy ones). Make Boolean Mesh writes the result into a new Part, one undo step, with options to weld the seams, keep each source's face groups and give the cut faces a face group of their own. The Boolean is exact (watertight when the Parts are; faces away from the cut, with their face groups, vertex paint and UVs, are kept as they are; flush and coplanar faces handled), with a voxel fallback for Parts that aren't closed (the status line says which it used). Saved in projects. Commands part_boolean, make_boolean_mesh, boolean_parts (scripts, Python, MCP). Requested by foirgairwolf and GABO on Discord.
  • "My Panel (Edit > My Panel; Requested by Hameron): hold Alt and drag a button or a section's title from any palette or shelf into a panel of your own; a section keeps all its live controls. It sits in a tray or its own window like any palette, or floats at the cursor on F4 (rebindable; Esc closes it). Alt+drag reorders, dragging an entry out or right-click removes it, and it is saved with the layout."
  • "Smooth Peaks brush: smooths like Smooth, but only brings down the vertices that sit above the average of their neighbours (along their normal); valleys are never filled. Works on the mesh and on micro levels, with masks, symmetry and alphas. Shift-smooth still uses the plain Smooth. Requested by ABHITAR."
  • Strands (Tool > Tube): Rope and Braid take 1 to 8 strands (3 as before); a rope of one strand is a spring, and Spread opens it. tube_set and tube_new take strands.
  • Repeat along curve (Tool > Tube, with a Tube or Curve Part active): pick another Part and its copies are laid end to end along the curve as a new Part, with Spacing (1 end to end, less overlaps them like chain links) and Turn (each copy turned that many degrees more than the one before; 90 for chain links). One undo step; the curve and the Part are kept. New command tube_repeat. Requested by Artizmo on Discord.
  • A leaner Welcome: about half the words, the 10-minute lesson first with the Quick tour beside it, the same looks, keys, starter meshes and AI On/Off. The privacy line is one sentence ("Your art is never uploaded or used for training.") with Details for the full text. Beside the User Guide, small grey icons for Discord, GitHub, X, Bluesky, Instagram and Facebook (also in the About header): a click opens that page in your browser, and the app makes no request to any of them on its own.
  • Layout autosave (thanks raffaele_3d_design on Discord). ui.json keeps the layout in use ("layout") and the Save Layout one ("layoutSaved"); older files read as both. Revert to Saved Layout returns only the layout, not shortcuts or preferences. Reset Layout, --reset-layout and Reset Layout and Shortcuts still win, and Revert still returns to the Save Layout one afterwards. The console, Library and Customize Shelves being open are not part of it. ui.prev.json and ui.prev2.json keep the two copies of ui.json from before the last sessions that changed the layout.
Changed
  • Braid strands are now flat ribbons that pass over and under each other instead of three round strands like a rope. A saved braid keeps its stored mesh until the tube is edited, then it is rebuilt in the new look. Requested by Artizmo on Discord.
  • The membership links in the app (Become a member, the yearly Member checkout, Founding Studio) carry a source tag, client_reference_id=app-card, so a checkout started in the app is attributed to it. Nothing else is sent; no tracking, no new preferences.
Fixed
  • Layout edits (Customize Shelves, trays, palettes) were lost on quit, a crash or Revert unless Save Layout was pressed first (reported by raffaele_3d_design on Discord).

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.summary: Added Garments: drape on the body (Tool > Garments > Drape on the body, garment_place, garment_drape): each panel placed by a click on the body (in front of it, facing the view; Turn, Wrap, Gap), saved with the pattern; the sewn pattern simulated live on the…
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Added
  • Garments: drape on the body (Tool > Garments > Drape on the body, garment_place, garment_drape): each panel placed by a click on the body (in front of it, facing the view; Turn, Wrap, Gap), saved with the pattern; the sewn pattern simulated live on the visible Parts (rest shape = the flat pattern, seams pulled shut).
  • Garments: Convert to Part: the draped garment as the Part "Garment": seams welded, UVs from the flat pattern, the pattern's thickness, one undo step.
  • "Save Visible Parts As... (File): saves a new .sfproj with only the visible Parts (their materials, layers, folders and linked copies kept, the cameras and settings too). The open project and its file stay as they are. Parts with streamed detail need Save As for now. Requested by phoenix."
  • Featured creator card in the Welcome window: a picture, the video's title and creator, and Watch (opens the browser; no embedded player). The list is featured.json beside latest.json on the same host, read with the daily update check and kept with its thumbnails in the preferences folder; a different entry each start, the x hides one for good. Watch links go only to https youtube.com, youtu.be and vimeo.com, thumbnails only from sculptforge.app; nothing is shown when the list is empty, the site can't be reached or update checks are off. First featured: askNK.
  • Reset Layout (Preferences > Saving & Layouts, command palette): the built-in shelves and trays with every panel back in the main window, shortcuts and preferences kept. sculptforge --reset-layout does the same at start. A shelf widget (colour picker, brush tiles, sliders) taken off a shelf is listed there with a Put back button.
  • Mask colour (Edit > Preferences > Interface): choose the colour masked areas show in the viewport; Mask darkness sets how much of it shows, Reset goes back to the default darkening look. Saved in the preferences. Requested by ABHITAR.
Changed
  • Startup splash: the start-up is also checked just before the first frame (a slow first frame or panel restore showed no splash), and once the splash is up it stays at least 0.7 s so it is seen, not flashed. A start that is over within 0.3 s still shows no splash and gets no added wait. SF_SPLASH=1 (environment variable) shows it on that run whatever the start-up time or the preference, for 0.7 s at least, to see it on a fast computer.
Fixed
  • Alt+click to select a Part (also Triple-click and Alt+Q) often missed thin, small or distant Parts, and a trackpad click that moved 4 points began a stroke instead. The pick now takes a Part within 8 points of the pointer when it is in front of the Part being sculpted, and a click may move 6 points (reported by phoenix on macOS).
  • Drape: cloth resting on a faceted body no longer creeps sideways
  • Drape on a figure modelled in centimetres or millimetres (the Full Body starter, most scans): the Units per metre slider now starts from the size of the scene (centimetres above 20 units tall, millimetres above 600) instead of 1, so the cloth falls and folds at a real-world speed instead of as if the figure were 100 times its size. Move the slider to set it yourself; the cloth_drape command still defaults to 1.
  • A project whose Part list is empty no longer fails with "Project has no valid Part list"; it opens as an empty scene (settings, lights, cameras, views and shelves load) and saves back the same.
  • The guide's 3D printing section pointed to File > Bridge > Export STL; Export STL is under File > Export.
  • Pan and zoom keys did nothing (0.12.5: the keys' glide ran in the test runner's frame loop only, never in the app's own; reported by Artizmo on Discord). A tap now moves the view about a tenth of a second's worth, a hold glides, on the default and on rebound keys. Tests: ui_key_nav_loop drives the app's real loop (--measure-key-nav), ui_key_nav the rest.
  • Revert to Saved Layout, Reset Layout and Import Interface run between frames instead of inside the palette that asked, so they can no longer swap the layout under it (reported by phoenix and raffaele_3d_design on macOS, Discord). Unsaved work is autosaved first; the first autosave of a session keeps the previous session's as autosave.prev.sfproj (Library > QuickSave), and the Restore prompt offers it.
  • Vertex paint lost on a subdivision round trip: fine colour painted at the highest level was overwritten with the interpolated low-level colour after painting at a lower level and stepping back up. A low-level stroke now goes up as a blended delta added to the colour the higher levels already hold (vertex paint, Base and paint layers). Undo across levels and Voxel Remesh colour transfer are covered by tests. Reported by masterfull95 on Discord.

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.summary: Added Startup splash: when start-up takes longer than about 0.3 s, a small window with the SculptForge bust, the wordmark and the version shows until the main window has drawn its first frame; the main window starts hidden instead of empty. Never in headless…
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Added
  • Startup splash: when start-up takes longer than about 0.3 s, a small window with the SculptForge bust, the wordmark and the version shows until the main window has drawn its first frame; the main window starts hidden instead of empty. Never in headless runs, tests or benchmarks (SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER=offscreen). Preferences > Interface > Show startup splash (on by default). Splash design idea by @lowenski (#176).
Changed
  • Pan and zoom keys (Ctrl+Numpad 4, 6, 8, 2, Zoom in/out) glide: a held key eases in and out (about 0.12 s each) and moves by speed x time every frame, so a 1-second hold covers the same distance at 30 and 144 fps, instead of a step, a quarter-second pause and then the hold. No OS key repeat is involved (requested by Artizmo on Discord).
  • The guide's Welcome chapter says membership early builds (each release about two weeks early) start with SculptForge 2027, the name of the official launch. Version numbers are unchanged.
  • Testing: end-to-end modelling scenarios (tests/e2e) run inside the existing test suites: sculpting, Voxel Remesh at 2M triangles, Extract, shelves, paint, tubes, cloth, Parts, export round trips, preferences and quitting. Nothing changes in the app.
Fixed
  • Generate 3D: when a free Hugging Face model finishes without a model, or refuses the job, the panel now says so in red under Generate, with the service name (it used to show only in the status bar, so it looked silent). Text to 3D on the two free Hunyuan3D Spaces is switched off by their owners; the message says that and points to Image to 3D or another provider. Photos from the phone use the same message.
  • Member builds (Preferences > Updates): the GitHub sign-in always ends with a visible message, including an account that is not yet on the member list or has an invitation to accept, a declined sign-in and an expired code (reported by a member). The sign-in's polling also retries a GitHub 5xx or rate limit instead of stopping. The device flow is now one tested function (all outcomes, slow_down, expiry, cancel).
  • Quitting with Alt+F4 on Linux (#183, X11): the window now stays until Alt and F4 are released (2 seconds at most). Closed while they were still down, the held key repeat or the release reached the desktop behind it, where Alt+F4 can be Log out. Stopping a helper program (splat trainer, COLMAP, ffmpeg) also can only signal that helper now: never our own process group, never everything (a pid of 0 or -1), never one that was already gone.
  • With Rgb on, a Sub stroke (Alt, or Sub toggled) laid no colour: it painted back towards white instead, so only Add strokes coloured the Part. Sub now lays the colour like Add, with the same alpha and Colour intensity, for every brush and stroke type. The Paint brush itself still paints back to white on Alt.
  • A custom brush lost from the bottom shelf (rand_gogh): a slot whose brush wasn't loaded kept its name and looked usable. It now shows a missing mark with a tooltip, finds the brush again if its file comes back (or is in the new backups folder), and Remove from shelf clears it.
  • Brush files are saved more safely: a save that doesn't fully reach the disk no longer replaces the good file, the file being replaced and a deleted brush are copied to backups/ in the brush library first, a brush file that can't be read is kept (and listed) and restored from that copy, and brushes that exist only in this session survive a library reload (installing or switching a pack).
  • Thread count capped at 16 (#184): a Threads value set by hand (Preferences > Performance, or set_performance_override threads) above 16 is used at the next start, up to the computer's hardware threads; the default is still every hardware thread up to 16. The paint-layer, transform, multires and texture loops follow the same count.

Added
  • Curve Part (Tool > Tube > Result > Curve; tube_new curve=true): a guide line drawn on or over the surface, with editable points, Resample (tube_resample count=N, exactly N evenly spaced points) and Tube from curve (tube_from_curve), which uses the Tube tool's sweep. Requested by Hameron (FXiT), GABO and Artizmo.
  • Origin tools in the Gizmo panel (requested by Ziel on Discord, with the Origin tools idea from @Devon0209): Center on origin moves the Part's bounding-box centre to 0,0,0 and Drop to floor rests its lowest point on Y = 0, each one undo step per Part, with All Parts together. Also the commands center_on_origin and drop_to_floor for scripts and the AI assistant.
  • Frame keys (idea by fenix on Discord): with the Classic sculpting keys and more than one Part, F frames the active Part and F twice within Frame double-tap (Preferences > Input, 400 ms, 0 = off) frames the whole scene. A scene with one Part frames as before. Frame scene is a bindable action.
  • Unlit view (#168, thanks @nagdav853): Alt+L, Render > Materials > Unlit and the right shelf's View list (set_unlit; the right shelf has no room for another default button, but Customize can add one) show vertex paint, texture paint and the PBR base colour with no lighting, Lit Sphere or PBR shading. The mask tint and wireframe still draw; the status bar shows Unlit while it is on. Saved with the project.
  • Wood brush pack (a seventh built-in pack, ten brushes: Weathered Planks, Raised Grain, Splinters, Wood Chaff, Grain Cracks, Check Split, Knot, End Rings, Plank Seams, Board Gap) with six new procedural alphas (Weathered Grain, Splinters, Grain Cracks, Knot, End Rings, Plank Seams) that work with any brush. Requested by Hameron (FXiT).
Fixed
  • Customize Shelves (Ctrl+Alt+drag): buttons that don't apply right now (the Front option, Vertex / Texture paint without a texture) and the shelf's value fields (Size, Intensity, Detail) can be moved again. Reported by fenix on Discord and MasterFULL on Discord.
  • Right shelf with the console open: the view toggles fold into the View button only when the shelf really is too short, and unfold only for a taller shelf; the buttons grow back only for a taller shelf, so the shelf should hold still (reported by Hameron (FXiT); please say if it still moves).
  • Drape: sewn seams stay closed where the cloth rests on the body (a T-shirt's waist and armpit seams stay within about 4 mm instead of opening to 6-9 mm), and a drape with one particle flipping between two spots a millimetre apart now comes to rest.
  • Shift-smooth used the wrong Intensity (#180, thanks @nekirk11): Shift with Drag Stamp strokes smoothed at the main brush's Intensity instead of Smooth's own, and the Intensity slider turned back to the main value as soon as the stroke began (so Smooth Intensity 10 looked like 80). Every stroke type now reads Smooth's value when Shift made it a smooth stroke.
  • Stencil in the SculptForge layout: Sculpt > Alpha > Stencil shows Adjust and Tile again, and the Remove (X) button (they sat past the panel's right edge, so only the Classic layout had them). Thanks MasterFULL on Discord.

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.title: SculptForge v0.12.1
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.summary: Added Focus Detail in projects: Divide to Micro past 300 million micro triangles streams the new level from a detail file (.sfdetail) instead of holding it all in memory; full detail loads where you look and sculpt. Save writes <project>.sfdetail beside the…
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Added
  • Focus Detail in projects: Divide to Micro past 300 million micro triangles streams the new level from a detail file (.sfdetail) instead of holding it all in memory; full detail loads where you look and sculpt. Save writes <project>.sfdetail beside the .sfproj (only the changed tiles, compacted once half the file is garbage) and opening the project streams from it again. Project format 9 (only for projects with a streamed level). Linux and macOS for now: Windows keeps such levels in memory, and a project with a streamed level opens on Linux and macOS only until Windows streaming lands.
  • Panels in their own windows (multi-monitor): any palette, the User Guide and Controls open in a window of their own from the new icon in their header or toolbar, to keep on another monitor or a pen display. Where each window was is remembered between sessions (per computer, panels.json, not in shared interface files); a monitor that has gone brings the panel back beside the main window. Shortcuts keep working while a panel window has the keyboard. Reset panel windows (Preferences > Saving & Layouts, command palette; also part of Reset Layout and Shortcuts) puts every panel back. On Wayland the compositor places the windows (their size is remembered, not their position). Requested by Richard Throgmorton (MakIt3D), Founding Member #1's Member Request.
  • Voxel Remesh up to 4096 (foirgairwolf on Discord): Tool > Remesh > Resolution and the remesh command go from 32 to 4096 (was 512). The slider keeps two thirds of its travel for 32-512 and a sixth each for 528-2048 and 2112-4096; Ctrl+click types a number. Above 512 only the voxels near the surface are stored (8x8x8 bricks), so memory grows with the surface, not the volume, and the result is the same surface the full grid would make. A sculpted head remeshes at 1024 into about 5.6M triangles in about 3 s, at 2048 into about 22M in about 9 s.
  • Triangle estimate under the Voxel Remesh Resolution slider (About 1.6M triangles), live as it moves; above 512 it also shows the memory needed, in red when more than is free.
  • High resolution remesh confirmation: the first remesh above 512 shows the estimated triangles and memory (Remesh / Cancel); it asks again after the Resolution goes back to 512 or less. A remesh that won't fit in the free memory doesn't start (the app and the remesh command both say how much it needs); it is cancellable with progress throughout.
  • Voxel Remesh, Quad Remesh and Decimate ask before they drop your subdivision levels ("This drops 3 subdivision levels"), with Freeze Levels and Proceed or Cancel, and Don't ask again. Nothing changes on a Part without levels. Thanks @TheLycanFenrir (#173).
Changed
  • Forge Spheres Draw builds without switching modes: a click on a sphere grows a new one, a drag on its body moves it and a drag on its rim resizes it (the cursor and a tag beside it say which); each drag is one undo step. Move and Scale work as before, and Drag places child (or Ctrl+drag) still grows and places a new sphere in one drag. Thanks @tristratos (#167)
  • Founding Studio is now for the first 5 studios (was 10): a flat $150 a month, locked, on the Help > Support card, the user guide's Studio membership and docs/studios.md.
  • Keyboard and mouse guide: Option is Alt on macOS, and how to make Option Alt and Cmd Ctrl when the Windows version runs under CrossOver or Wine on a Mac (their Mac driver sends Cmd as Alt by default; thanks @fenixpoints).
  • Focus Detail (experimental, --focus-detail): the GPU now keeps a small record per tile (coarse grid and edges) and full-resolution grids only for the tiles drawn close up, within a fixed pool; coarse tiles are shaded at their own level, so a streamed level opens shaded at once instead of shading every full grid first.
  • Website: the Membership page thanks every Founding Member by their credit name (the same list as the Members page), and build_site.py --supporters rewrites that line with the list, so a newly credited founder shows up in both.
Fixed
  • Focus Detail: saving a project with a streamed level kept only the coarse detail; bake, displacement export, surface noise and copies of a streamed level now use full detail.
  • Find Problems > Fix all left non-manifold edges and opened holes on messy meshes, such as a rough remesh (foirgairwolf on Discord). Solids touching along an edge now come apart closed, Fix all repeats until only holes are left, the Holes Fix never makes other problems or leaves more holes than it found, and the panel says what couldn't be fixed and why. The inner wall of a hollow (or an eye inside a head) is no longer counted as flipped.
  • Alpha stamps leaving gaps on curved meshes (#174, thanks @Devon0209): a large Drag Stamp or Slide Stamp (any alpha, sculpt or paint) only reached the vertices within its radius in space, so where the surface curved away from the view part of the stamp's footprint stayed untouched. The stamp now also takes the visible surface under its footprint.
  • Clay, Clay Block, Flatten and Trim on micro levels have a safeguard against stretched triangles on big moves: points facing away from the brush plane stay put, and no point moves more than a quarter of the brush per dab. Ordinary strokes look and feel the same.
  • Drape settles where it used to keep twitching: cloth pressed into a narrow fold of the body (an armpit, the inside of an elbow) stays put instead of bouncing between the two sides, and sewn seams no longer pull the cloth through the body while they close. It now runs until the cloth has really stopped, which can take a moment longer (still under 10 s for a 2M-triangle body).
  • Solo in the Parts panel now remembers which Parts were shown when it began and restores exactly those on exit, so Parts hidden beforehand stay hidden (also across save and load while in Solo). Thanks MasterFULL on Discord

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.title: SculptForge v0.12.0
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.summary: Added A first-use notice before the first request to each third-party AI host (Pollinations.ai, each Hugging Face Space family, fal.ai, Meshy, Hyper3D, a remote OpenAI-compatible server or ComfyUI), drawn inside the AI Brush or Generate 3D panel (no dialog):…
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Added
  • A first-use notice before the first request to each third-party AI host (Pollinations.ai, each Hugging Face Space family, fal.ai, Meshy, Hyper3D, a remote OpenAI-compatible server or ComfyUI), drawn inside the AI Brush or Generate 3D panel (no dialog): what is sent, the host, who pays, and Allow / Use local instead (a running Ollama, LM Studio or ComfyUI) or Set up local / Cancel. Nothing is sent before Allow: the request functions refuse on their own, so scripts, sculptforge-cli and AI tools get the same refusal until the service is allowed in the app. Allow is kept per service in ai.json (sendAllowed); Preferences > AI > Online AI services lists each one as Allowed, Asks first, or set by the studio, with Revoke. Servers on this computer (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) never ask. A studio policy pre-allows what its ai.providers / ai.endpoints list and its "no" wins over an artist's Allow. The guide's interface chapter has a plain "What leaves your computer" table. No new network host, key or server.
  • Cloth brush: simulates the surface near the stroke as fabric (our own XPBD cloth solver, docs/design/cloth.md): Drag pulls it along and it buckles into folds that keep their length, Push presses it in (Alt pulls), Settle drapes it under gravity, Grab holds what it took and drags it (Move-like), Expand / Pinch spread or gather it, Inflate adds fabric so it balloons and wrinkles. Soft body springs it back toward its shape; self-collision keeps folds from passing through each other. Fabric presets Silk, Cotton, Denim and Leather; collides with the other visible Parts; masked areas hold like pins; symmetry, sculpt layers, one undo step per stroke. Asked for on YouTube.
  • Drape (Tool > Drape, cloth_drape): the active Part simulated as cloth (our XPBD solver) until it rests on the other visible Parts; fabric presets, real-size scale (units per metre), pins from the mask, Simulate / Pause / Keep / Reset with a live view, one undo step. The cloth doesn't pass through thin, sharp shapes (needle tips, fingers, curls) or through the body when it falls fast. Tip: drop the cloth from in front of overhanging shapes (beards, chins), or it settles behind them.
  • Crease / Uncrease in Tool > Geometry > Edges (#108): a crease value (0..1, 1 = fully sharp) on the selected edges of the base level, one undo step each, saved in the project (an optional blob: older versions open the file without creases) and kept on the base while stepping levels. Creased edges are drawn in blue on the base level in every mode. The edge_crease command does the same from scripts. Add Level honours creases (Catmull-Clark and Loop semi-sharp creases: sharpness 10 x crease², s - 1 per level, fractional blending): creasing at Level 1 under existing levels reshapes them with their detail; Remove Below keeps what is left of the creases on the new base. Without creases subdivision is bit-for-bit unchanged. USD export / import carries them (creaseIndices / creaseLengths / creaseSharpnesses, subdivisionScheme catmullClark or loop on a creased cage); glTF, OBJ, FBX, PLY and STL have none (documented). Thanks _tfx on Discord for asking; the plan for edge creases is @NicTanghe's (#108).
  • Edges mode (Tool > Geometry > Edges, #108): picks edges of a Part's base level (Level 1; a Part with levels steps down to it) on the model: click selects the edge under the cursor, Shift+click adds, Ctrl+click removes, a double-click takes the edge loop (across quads, or along an open border). Select by Angle selects the edges whose faces meet at more than the Angle (30 degrees by default), optionally only within the selection; Grow, Shrink, Open Edges, Invert and Deselect All. Quad diagonals are never edges. The edge_select command does the same from scripts. Thanks _tfx on Discord for asking for select by angle; the plan for edge creases is @NicTanghe's (#108). Creases themselves come next.
  • Pattern window: Templates and Print (Tool > Garments): Templates lists the T-shirt, trousers, straight and A-line skirts, hoodie, dress, cloak and gloves, with Add beside the pattern for an outfit and an editable Size chart (mm) (hover a measurement to see how to take it); Print picks A4 or Letter, portrait or landscape, shows how many pages it takes, and saves one PDF or one SVG per page. Both open under their buttons. Spanish and Chinese included.
  • Garments, part 2: the Pattern window (Tool > Garments > Pattern): the garment's panels flat at real size over a 10 / 100 mm grid with a scale bar. Start from a T-shirt or a rectangle, or import an SVG; drag points (snapping to the 5 mm grid and other panels' points; Ctrl drags freely), curve handles or whole panels; Alt+click an edge to add a point, Delete removes it, C curves an edge. Sew by clicking two edges: every seam is listed by its edges' names ("Front left side <-> Back left side") with both lengths, green when they match, red when one side is eased in; hover a seam or an edge to see what it is sewn to. Duplicate, Mirror Copy (the other sleeve), Mirror, rename, particle distance, fabric and thickness; export SVG or DXF. Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z over the window undo and redo pattern edits. In English, Spanish and Chinese.
  • Garment templates (#garments): trousers, straight and A-line skirts (with waistband), hoodie (long sleeves, two-piece hood, kangaroo pocket), dress (bodice and A-line skirt), cloak (half-circle cape with hood) and gloves (a pair), next to the T-shirt. Flat panels at real size from a size chart saved in the project (chest, waist, hip, neck, shoulder, arm, inseam, rise, head, hand and more: garment_size), sewn the way each garment is made with the seam lengths matched; garment_new template=... add=true builds an outfit in one pattern. Our own proportions, documented in docs/design/garment-templates.md. Their seams read by name in the Pattern window ("Left front inseam <-> Left back inseam", "Left sleeve cuff <-> ..."), as the T-shirt's do; mirrored panels keep the names. Printing patterns at home: garment_export writes tiled PDF (or one SVG per page) for A4 or Letter, portrait or landscape: trim lines, half triangles that complete across each join, page names (A1, A2, ... B1), the 50 mm check square on A1; blank pages are left out and a mirrored or repeated piece prints once, marked "cut 2, 1 reversed". The whole-sheet SVG and the DXF for cutters stay. Guide chapter Garments.
  • Generate 3D candidates: Candidates (1-3) makes several shapes in one go, side by side as a shaded thumbnail over a flat black silhouette, so the strongest form is picked before any sculpting. Free and local services start at 3; fal.ai, Meshy and Hyper3D start at 1 (each candidate is one generation on your own key, and the window says how many are billed). The pick becomes a Part (only an untouched untitled scene is replaced); the others are discarded or, with Keep the others as hidden Parts, kept hidden. "Same shape as A" when a service returns one shape twice.
  • Use as sculpting base (Generate 3D): one click after picking runs Voxel Remesh, then Quad Remesh (Then Quad Remesh, on by default), for a clean, even mesh with one subdivision level. Keep a high-detail copy (hidden) keeps the model as generated as a hidden Part below it; Project Detail from the high-detail copy brings its detail back after Add Level.
  • Pose all Parts (Tool > Parts, figure_pose_begin / figure_pose_apply / figure_pose_cancel): the visible Parts become one light Pose Mesh (each Part reduced to its share of 300k triangles, one face group per Part, so Mask by Face group picks Parts; a Part with subdivision levels joins from a lower level, so it is ready in seconds). Pose it with the Gizmo, masks, soft joints and symmetry; Undo steps back through the pose. Apply Pose moves every Part at full resolution the same way (sculpt layers, subdivision and micro levels follow), as one undo step across all Parts; Cancel Pose leaves everything as it was. Requested by @ABHITAR.

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.summary: Added Gizmo All mode (Shift+W, top shelf, Sculpt > Symmetry & Gizmo; the gizmo_mode command): move, rotate and scale handles at once, with clear priorities where they cross and no overlaps at any zoom or UI scale. Snapping, the readout, posing with a mask,…
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Added
  • Gizmo All mode (Shift+W, top shelf, Sculpt > Symmetry & Gizmo; the gizmo_mode command): move, rotate and scale handles at once, with clear priorities where they cross and no overlaps at any zoom or UI scale. Snapping, the readout, posing with a mask, Alt+drag for the pivot and one undo step per drag work as in the single modes. Idea by fenix on Discord (thanks @fenixpoints, #118).
  • Keep original checkbox under Tool > Parts > Split (Hidden / Masked / Unmasked; keep=true on part_split_hidden, part_split_masked, part_split_unmasked): the triangles are copied into the new Part (UVs, face groups, vertex paint, sculpt layers; the copy is cut at the current subdivision level) and the source Part stays untouched, levels and mask included. One undo step removes the copy. Requested by _tfx on Discord.
  • Website: Most-wanted brushes on the brushes page (sculptforge.app/brushes.html#requests): brush requests from the #ideas forum on our Discord, ranked by 👍 votes and refreshed every 30 minutes, with shipped ones marked. The data is also published as sculptforge.app/brush-requests.json.
Changed
  • Release packages are built once per set of build inputs: a commit whose packaged files are byte for byte an earlier green build's (a website or release-paperwork change) reuses that build's packages, verified and attested as before, instead of building them again (docs/releasing.md, "Build once, promote").
  • Monthly challenge on Discord: submissions close on the 27th at 23:59, then everyone votes in a Discord poll until the end of the month; the winner (Featured Artist and a spot on sculptforge.app) is announced on the 1st. The website and the guide's Discord page say so.
  • Member builds in the app now come from the SculptForge organization; update to keep signing in.
  • Tool > Geometry is reorganised by task (Levels, Micro Detail, Resolution, Cleanup, Symmetry) with clearer names; your hotkeys, scripts and search keep working.
  • Membership wording in the app, the guide and the README now matches the membership page: Member Requests are one request a month, built first and credited to you (Help > Support, the welcome screen and the membership card; Spanish and Chinese too). Bugs are always free, and every idea goes in the public feature queue.
Fixed
  • Blender input style: Ctrl+Shift did nothing on the model (Ctrl is Blender's invert, so Ctrl+Shift became an inverted smooth), so the Cut shapes and the Ctrl+Shift hide/isolate gestures were out of reach. Ctrl+Shift now keeps its meaning in every style (drag: hide or cut; add Alt: inside / the other side; Ctrl+Shift+click the brush tile or Ctrl+Shift+B: the selection and Cut shapes). Ctrl alone still inverts, Shift alone still smooths. Alt+Q (pick the Part under the cursor, Blender's own key) is now listed with the Blender keys, since Alt+click masks there (thanks dm4nd on Discord).
  • Cut with symmetry on: a shape whose mirror image overlaps it (a rectangle across the middle, a centred one seen at an angle) sometimes cut one side only, In and Add went deeper on one side, and a later cut across those caps could leave a crack. The mirror image now measures its depth on the Part as it was, cuts stop at once instead of leaving one side done, and the zero-area slivers the overlap left in the cap are cleaned up so the next cut closes (thanks dm4nd on Discord).
  • Tool > Parts > Extract and Project labels were cut off in a narrow tray (since 0.11.11). The settings now read Thickness, Edge Smooth, Both Sides, Corners and Border; a pair shares a row only when both labels fit, else each takes its own, and Both Sides / Corners / Border wrap. Scripts use triangle_corners / triangle_border; the old argument and action names still work.
  • macOS: SculptForge > Preferences... in the app menu was greyed out; it now opens Preferences, as Cmd+, and Edit

    Preferences do (#111, thanks @fenixpoints).

  • Popups, menus, tooltips, the Command Palette, the Quick Menu and floating windows are fully opaque in every look (Classic, Forge Terminal and its schemes, Phosphor, Blueprint); at 200% the Preferences popup showed the Sculpt Timeline's "Save with project" and the shelf text through it. Overlays on the 3D view keep their translucency.

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.title: SculptForge v0.11.15
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.summary: Added Tube (Tool > Tube): draw tubes freely in 3D space, like a 3D pen. Strokes lie on a plane facing the view (at the surface where the stroke starts, the pivot, or a fixed distance), optionally snapped onto surfaces; pen pressure sets the radius and the…
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Added
  • Tube (Tool > Tube): draw tubes freely in 3D space, like a 3D pen. Strokes lie on a plane facing the view (at the surface where the stroke starts, the pivot, or a fixed distance), optionally snapped onto surfaces; pen pressure sets the radius and the stroke is smoothed into a curve. The tube is swept along it with rings placed closer in bends and frames that never twist, round or flat ends, and Symmetry X. Each stroke is a Tube Part whose points are dragged (Ctrl: thickness, Alt+click: delete), inserted and deleted until Bake, or goes straight into the active Part with even edge lengths for dynamic topology; one undo step each. Script and AI commands tube_new, tube_list, tube_set_point, tube_insert_point, tube_delete_point, tube_set, tube_bake. Guide chapter "Tube: draw in 3D space". Requested by GABO on Discord.
  • Hardware tiers (Edit > Preferences > Performance): the detected tier and why ("RTX 3060, 12 GB VRAM, 32 GB RAM: High"), what it turns on, Auto or any tier by hand. The Essential tier works exactly as before; Standard and up keep more Focus Detail in memory, and High and up allow 16K paint and bake textures. A small card on first launch (and after a hardware change) shows the tier once; the chip in the top bar opens the panel. A memory guard steps the tier down a level when free memory runs low, and back up when there is room. Turbo (the bolt in the top bar, View > Turbo, Ctrl+Alt+T): antialiasing off and a lighter view while you sculpt and orbit, the detected tier's top budgets; full quality when the view stops, and Off changes nothing you set. Remembered per computer. Graphics card picker on computers with two (applies on the next start, through the system's own setting; a card that fails to start falls back to the system's choice). Compute: Auto / CPU / GPU, with each task's path shown (all CPU for now). SF_HW_SIMULATE=floor|standard|high|extreme, SF_TIER_, SF_COMPUTE=cpu|gpu, SF_TURBO=1 for benches. Memory in the top bar, beside the triangles and frame rate: SculptForge's RAM and the system's free RAM, and the graphics card's memory in use where its driver reports it (NVIDIA; AMD shows what's free), updated once a second; hover for the detail. Thanks, Oslen on Discord.
  • Split > Hidden / Masked / Unmasked (Tool > Parts; part_split_hidden, part_split_masked, part_split_unmasked): the triangles leave the active Part for a new Part below it (same folder, visibility and shading), one undo step that also removes the new Part. A triangle is masked when its corners' average mask is above 50%. UVs, face groups, vertex paint and sculpt layers carry over; subdivision levels are cut at the current level (undo restores them). Thanks foirgairwolf on Discord.
  • Delete masked (Tool > Visibility; delete_masked), the mirror of Delete hidden. Thanks foirgairwolf on Discord.
  • A per-Part shading mark in the Parts list (Scene / Smooth / Flat; part_shading). Thanks foirgairwolf on Discord.
  • Merge by Distance (Tool > Geometry; weld_points distance=... preview=true): the points of the active Part within the distance merge into the nearest kept one; collapsed triangles go; one undo step. The count follows the slider and the points that would merge show in orange. Thanks foirgairwolf on Discord.
  • Check Mesh (Tool > Geometry; mesh_check, mesh_fix issue=...): non-manifold edges (Fix loosens the extra triangles), holes (capped as Close Holes), duplicate and degenerate triangles (deleted), zero-area triangles (shortest edge collapsed), flipped triangles and inside-out closed pieces (rewound), isolated points (removed). Fix all fixes everything except holes, as one undo step. Thanks foirgairwolf on Discord.
  • Recent colours (Oslen on Discord): under the left shelf's two swatches, the last eight paint colours a stroke or Fill used, newest first, in rows of four; click one to paint with it. Kept in the preferences, so they survive a restart.
  • View speed (Preferences > Tablet): how far the pen turns, pans and zooms the view per pixel, 0.10 to 2.00 (1.00, the default, moves it as the mouse does). A tablet spreads its whole area over the screen, so a short pen movement crosses many pixels and orbiting seemed far faster than with the mouse (Huion on Windows; thanks to GonzaloHernandez3D on Reddit). Saved in the preferences; Tablet defaults sets it back to 1.00.
Fixed
  • Holding a rebound Smaller brush / Larger brush key (and the 1 px Shift steps) repeats again, like [ and ] always did; after a rebind it changed the size once and stopped. Those keys also step through an insert set. Not while typing in a field (thanks Ziel on Discord).
  • Forge Spheres with Symmetry on: a new sphere placed near the centre line (closer than its own radius) now snaps onto it as one sphere instead of two overlapping twins that skinned as separate branches. Spheres growing from a mirrored arm or leg still get their twin (thanks dm4nd on Discord).
  • Frame (F, the Frame button), a new model and Reset View fit the model into the canvas the open Library and the Sculpt Timeline strip leave free: at 200 % on a 1080p screen the sphere's top sat under them. Opening or closing the Library doesn't move the view; the next Frame uses the new free area.
  • The left shelf's brush tiles and colour picker shrink to fit its column (and the wheel scrolls it past that): at 150 % on a 1080p screen the colour swatches ran under the bottom shelf.
  • Pen taps on menus and buttons work the first time, also a tap within one frame or right after the pen comes into range, with Windows Ink and with Huion's extra mouse events (reported by GonzaloHernandez3D on Reddit; fixed by the pen click rework in 0.10.9, now covered by a test).
  • Micro levels: big Clay, Clay Block, Flatten and Trim strokes on a Part with a Micro level could break the surface into shards across the whole brush (since 0.11.10), and sculpting there had become much slower on very dense meshes. Both are back to how 0.11.9 worked, and so is its one known issue: where several Clay strokes end on the same spot of a rough surface, a few short spikes can show. A proper fix for that comes in 0.11.16.
  • The side columns (the shelf with Undo and Redo, the brush and colour shelf) and the trays no longer scroll sideways. At some UI scales their tiles were a few pixels wider than the column, so a sideways swipe or scroll moved them; the tiles now fit the column and the trays only scroll up and down (dm4nd on Discord).

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.summary: Added Deformation stack (Tool > Deformation > Stack, requested by foirgairwolf on Discord): thirteen whole-Part shape operations in four groups (Transform: Move, Turn, Scale, Squash; Bend & Twist: Bend, Twist, Taper, Shear; Shape: Round, Box, Flatten, Sag,…
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Added
  • Deformation stack (Tool > Deformation > Stack, requested by foirgairwolf on Discord): thirteen whole-Part shape operations in four groups (Transform: Move, Turn, Scale, Squash; Bend & Twist: Bend, Twist, Taper, Shear; Shape: Round, Box, Flatten, Sag, Depth; plus the Surface ones), each along any of X, Y and Z about the Part's centre (or the gizmo's placed pivot), with Direction for Bend and Shear and Soft for an eased profile. The preview is the stack applied as one undo step and follows each change; Apply, Apply Selected, Reset and Repeat. The mask holds what it covers. Commands deform_move ... deform_depth and deform_stack for scripts and the AI.
  • Size (Tool > Deformation, requested by foirgairwolf on Discord): the active Part's X, Y and Z dimensions in scene units, to drag or type exactly; it resizes about its centre (Uniform: in proportion), one undo step. Command deform_size.
  • Top bar heart (Help > Support SculptForge); a small badge for verified members. Hidden in studio builds and before it would crowd a narrow top bar.
  • Note fragments take member_request: true (and member_credit: @handle when the member opted in): What's New tags the change "Requested by a member".
  • Website: Feature queue (sculptforge.app/queue.html, footer link on the membership page): every feature idea with its status (building, queued, shipped, already in the app, declined) and a member flag.
Changed
  • Blender add-on and Maya script have their own versions and can be released on their own, as soon as they change (GitHub releases blender-vX.Y.Z / maya-vX.Y.Z); the website's download links follow the newest one. The add-on is now 1.0.0 (it used to carry the app's version). Each SculptForge release still includes both.
  • Membership card: milestone moments (10th start, 10 hours of stroke time, 100th save; local counts only, nothing sent), an optional honest line from the update feed's support block (funded this month, Founding Members taken, member requests this release), and a backoff (monthly after the 3rd "Not now", only after an update after the 6th). Every existing rule stays: never modal, never mid-stroke or during a job, never in tests, renders or CI, never for members, at most once a week.
  • Compact bars (factoberplay on YouTube): the Library strip and the Sculpt Timeline take 158 logical px instead of 228 (31% less). The Library's thumbnails are 64 px by default (were 96) and its tab row 26 px; drag the strip's edge toward the canvas to size them (48-128 px, kept with the layout; also Edit > Preferences > Library > Thumbnails). The timeline is one row (step count, track, icon buttons) with thin branch lanes; the full strip with its header row comes back from the unfold icon or Edit > Preferences > Interface > Compact timeline.
  • The membership cards link to the membership terms (Terms & refunds, sculptforge.app/terms.html), and open only their fixed links.
  • The built-in Stone Carve brush (Sculpt > Brush, and the community gallery) has a name of our own. Shelves, key bindings, pie menus and scripts saved with its old name still find it.
  • Website: How requests work on the membership page (sculptforge.app/support.html#requests): bugs are always free; every idea goes in a public queue; members' requests are built first, one guaranteed request a month each (built and credited); Founding Members and Studio go first; a monthly member vote sets the order; popular ideas from everyone still get built. A "Built for members" list shows what member requests became.

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.title: SculptForge v0.11.13
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.summary: Added Generate 3D > Remove flat background (on by default): a thin wall behind or ground under the subject, covering most of the model's bounds, is removed from the generated mesh before remeshing, as its own undo step; a relief or a coin on its own is kept.…
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Added
  • Generate 3D > Remove flat background (on by default): a thin wall behind or ground under the subject, covering most of the model's bounds, is removed from the generated mesh before remeshing, as its own undo step; a relief or a coin on its own is kept. image_to_3d / text_to_3d take remove_background=false, and the new remove_flat_background command does it on the active Part. Requested by fenix on Discord.
  • Linked Duplicates (#94, asked for by ebarranco; the idea of placing copies on their own by NicTanghe): Tool > Parts > Linked Duplicate adds a Part sharing the active one's mesh, undo history and GPU buffers, with its own transform. Strokes, masking and painting on any copy edit the shared mesh (symmetry about the copy's own axes); the Gizmo and transform move a linked copy as a whole (a mask poses the shared mesh instead); Make Unique breaks the link; deleting one keeps the others. The Parts list shows a link and the count. Projects keep the links (project format 8); glTF reuses one mesh with a node per copy, USD writes instanceable prims referencing the first copy (and reads them back), OBJ / STL / FBX / PLY write each copy where it is. Commands part_duplicate_linked and part_make_unique. 500 linked copies use about the memory of one mesh.
  • Orbit lock (View > Orbit lock, a request from foirgairwolf on Discord): besides Free and Y (the turntable), rotation drags can turn the view about the world X or Z axis only, with no drift over long drags. A key for each (Alt+Shift+F / Y / X / Z) and the orbit_lock axis=free|y|x|z command; the axis gizmo draws the locked axis through its disc with a lock badge. Shift still snaps to side views. Saved with the preferences (also Preferences > Interface / Input > Rotation; older versions read Y as Turntable).
  • Website: Jobs (sculptforge.app/jobs.html, footer link): open sculpting and 3D modeling roles worldwide (games, film and VFX, animation, collectibles, 3D printing, jewelry and dental CAD, AR/VR) from the companies' own public job feeds, filtered by region, sector, role, Remote and contract. A daily GitHub Action (tools/jobs/fetch.py, sources in tools/jobs/studios.yaml) refreshes it; titles, companies and places only, never job descriptions.
Changed
  • The window title starts with the project name and a "*" for unsaved changes (taskbars stay readable), then SculptForge and its version, and the top bar shows the version, small and dim, beside the name in both layouts (a narrow window drops it). A narrow window or a high UI scale (a 1024 px window at 200 %) never draws top bar items over each other any more: the version goes first, then the layout presets and Save Snapshot, the search field shrinks to its icon, and the menus that don't fit open from a >> button. Betas show their tag ("0.12.0 beta.2") in the accent colour; builds from a git checkout show "dev" and their commit.
Fixed
  • The membership card now shows the Studio membership's flat price for any number of artists.
  • Reconstruct Subdiv (Tool > Geometry): the levels it builds keep each face inside one UV island when the imported high-poly's seams run through the lower level's faces (UVs made on the high-poly, automatic unwraps with overlapping islands). Such faces used to take each corner's UV from a different island and stretch across UDIM tiles. Reconstructing again on such a mesh also finds the right lower level now. Thanks @RodTDai for the report, the screenshots and the diagnosis that pointed to the fix (#145).
  • Timelapse: a PBR timelapse of a high-detail sculpt flickered a little in the video (not in the view): after each step of the history the frames switched between the full mesh and its lighter preview levels. Timelapse frames and --render turntables now always draw the full mesh. Thanks @ebarranco.
  • The Sculpt Timeline strip's header no longer runs under Save with project in a narrow window or at a high UI scale (a 1024 px window at 200 %): the step count, branches, step name and message are shortened with "..." to fit.
  • Member builds sign-in accepts GitHub's longer tokens (its new ~520-character format, and up to 4096 characters): before, a long token was refused and the sign-in failed without a word. On Windows, where one Credential Manager entry holds at most 2560 bytes, a longer sign-in is kept across several entries (studio sign-ins too); sign-ins stored by earlier versions still load.

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.title: SculptForge v0.11.12
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.summary: Added Garments, part 1 (scripting and the AI assistant for now; the Pattern window follows): pattern panels at real size (millimetres, curves, notches, grain line, seam allowance) saved in the project, a T-shirt template (front, back, two sleeves, sewn), seams…
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Added
  • Garments, part 1 (scripting and the AI assistant for now; the Pattern window follows): pattern panels at real size (millimetres, curves, notches, grain line, seam allowance) saved in the project, a T-shirt template (front, back, two sleeves, sewn), seams with length and direction checks, even triangulation at a chosen particle distance with seams matched point for point, export as a real-size SVG for printing and sewing (with a 50 mm scale square) or DXF for cutters, and SVG panels read back in. Commands: garment_new, garment_info, garment_add_panel, garment_sew, garment_export, garment_import and more.
Changed
  • The app icon is the orange outline cube again, as it was before 0.11 (window, taskbar, dock, Start menu, Linux packages).
  • Linux packaging: every AppImage build checks that it starts on 4, 16 and 64 KiB memory pages (no bundled jemalloc, 64 KiB ELF alignment on ARM64). On Apple Silicon Linux (Asahi) the guide points to the ARM64 build: the x86_64 one runs there only through the FEX emulator, whose own jemalloc stops with "Unsupported system page size".
  • Maya Live link (#42): on very large meshes the mid-stroke updates to Maya come less often (at most about 4% of the app's time), so sculpting stays smooth; the link is now tested on Windows' named pipe as well.
  • A check (tools/check_public_email.py, in CI and the test suite) keeps our email address off the website, docs and README.
  • Site: Richard Throgmorton (MakIt3D) is credited as our first Founding Member (members page, membership page; Help > About in the next app build).
  • Site: favicons and the press kit's app icon are the orange outline cube again, as it was before 0.11.
  • Guide: SculptForge installs from FlatPark (x86_64 and ARM64) and then updates with flatpak update; the package table, the Flatpak section and the press kit's platform list say so.
  • Site: our email address is no longer in any public page; the Studios page's "Start a Studio membership" and "email us" links build it when clicked (Discord without JavaScript), and the guide points to the SculptForge Discord.
  • Studio membership is now a flat $300 a month for the whole studio, any number of artists (no per-artist charge); Founding Studio is a flat $150 a month for the first 10 studios. The Studios and Membership pages get a direct "Studio: $300 / month" checkout button.
Fixed
  • Text people type (Part, folder, layer and brush-set names, file names, Library items, pasted text) with a character outside the bundled fonts drew as "?": the Chinese fonts carry only the interface's own characters. Such a character is now taken from the system's fonts the first time it is drawn (Windows: Microsoft YaHei, JhengHei, Yu Gothic, Malgun Gothic; macOS: PingFang, Hiragino, Apple SD Gothic Neo; Linux: fontconfig, e.g. Noto Sans CJK), including characters past U+FFFF such as 𠀋. Nothing is loaded while no such text is shown, and the interface uses about 15 MB less memory (the fonts are no longer copied per size). Shortened names (the title bar) no longer end in a broken character when cut in Chinese.
  • The new-version notice in a Flatpak from FlatPark shows flatpak update (with a Copy button) instead of telling you to download a new file.
  • Focus Detail (experimental, --focus-detail): the app loop now loads full detail where the camera looks (it only did in UI tests); a stroke that widened the displacement range left the tiles not yet loaded at the old scale (they now follow, and Save writes them at the new scale).
  • macOS: the app's small icon (Finder's Get Info thumbnail, list view, 16 and 32 px) was noise; the .icns now stores those sizes in the classic RGB + mask form Finder draws everywhere (#156, thanks @tristratos).
  • The window's size and place and project.json (recent files, Discord and autosave settings) are written to a temporary file and then renamed, so a quit that ends mid-write (a stalled disk) keeps the last whole copy.
  • Linux AppImage: after Restart to update, the previous version hid its window and never quit, so it kept running in the background (and, with Show SculptForge on Discord on, kept "Playing SculptForge" on your profile after you closed SculptForge). It now quits as soon as the new version is up. Updating from 0.11.10 or earlier, the new version ends the previous one itself (thanks @ebarranco).
  • Show SculptForge on Discord: quitting clears it first and it never comes back during the teardown; a quit that stalls ends the process after 15 s; the status shows the outline cube icon instead of the old SF letters.
  • SpaceMouse: turning the cap slowly no longer ends in a zoom that flies the view away (3DxWare's scrolling got through while the cap was inside the dead zone, and just after the cap was let go). Thanks @fenixpoints.
  • Stencil edges sculpt as clean grooves instead of a beaded zipper: a built-in pattern made into a Stencil (Use alpha) is generated again at 1024 px instead of the alpha's 128, whose pixels showed as stair-steps along every edge it sculpted.

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.summary: Added Brush sets (#143, asked for by @NicTanghe): Sculpt > Brush > Brush set > Save keeps the bottom shelf's brushes, in order, and their keys as a named set in your brush library; picking a set (the Brush palette, the bottom shelf's right-click menu Brush…
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Added
  • Brush sets (#143, asked for by @NicTanghe): Sculpt > Brush > Brush set > Save keeps the bottom shelf's brushes, in order, and their keys as a named set in your brush library; picking a set (the Brush palette, the bottom shelf's right-click menu Brush set, or Brush Set: Wood in the command palette) swaps the shelf and the keys in one step, and the set you switched to comes back at the next start. Custom and pack brushes on the bottom shelf can now hold a key too (Ctrl+Alt+click the tile, then press the key). Commands: brush_set, brush_set_save, brush_set_delete.
  • Creature bones (Append > Insert on the model, #154): a built-in insert set of 13 original fantasy creature bones (Skull, Jaw, Fang, Blade tooth, Swept horn, Spiral horn, Claw, Vertebra, Tail vertebrae, Rib, Limb bone, Wing bone, Wing finger), clean closed quad meshes for dividing and sculpting, generated in-house by tools/creature-bones. Commands: insert_set_items set=builtin:creature-bones, insert_mesh set=builtin:creature-bones index=<n>. Translated piece names. Thanks @kenttumanda123-netizen.
  • Floor grid (#115, View > Floor grid, also Tool > Display and the command palette): a faint grid on the floor under the model (its lowest point, Y up; it moves when a stroke or a move ends), the X and Z axes through the origin marked, squares stepping by ten with the zoom and fading into the distance. It never draws over the model. Off by default; remembered in the preferences. Suggested by @fenixpoints.
  • Maya Live (#42, thanks @tristratos): File > Maya > Live sends the Parts a stroke, undo or edit changed to the exchange folder by itself once the scene is still for 300 ms (never mid-stroke), written in the background; the Maya shelf's new Live button does the same for Maya edits (node-dirty callbacks, debounced). Echo guard: manifests carry the writer's session id, a Get is never sent back, and an object that comes back unchanged is skipped (no undo step). Both sides pick up sends every 250 ms (was once a second); OBJs are written to a temporary name and renamed.
  • Maya Live link (#42): opt-in, off at every start and never remembered; a warning every time it is turned on; an ember Live link on chip in the top bar (and the Forge status bar) turns it off. A per-user Unix socket or named pipe (never a TCP or UDP port), a 128-bit pairing code (File > Maya > Copy pairing code, pasted into the shelf's new Link button), one client at a time, mesh data only in strictly parsed frames (1 GiB cap, timeouts, fuzz-tested). SculptForge streams the vertices a stroke moves about ten times a second and sends whole meshes when faces change; Maya edits come back as whole meshes. Studios can forbid it with "maya": {"link": "never"}. Guide: Working with Maya > Live, Live link.
  • Stencil (Sculpt > Alpha > Stencil, #155, thanks @kenttumanda123-netizen): an image over the view (loaded like an alpha, or the brush's alpha) that the brushes work through. It stays put on screen while the model turns under it; every brush that takes an alpha (built-in, custom and Community brushes, the Paint brush, micro levels) takes its brightness (sculpt) or its colours (Vertex Paint, or its brightness masking the paint colour) at the place each vertex shows, and nothing off the image. Adjust: drag to move, a corner to scale, the round handle to turn; arrows,
    • =, , . on the keyboard. Invert, Tile, Opacity, Hide while navigating. Symmetry mirrors it. Commands stencil_load, stencil_set, stencil_clear. Texture painting doesn't take it yet.
Changed
  • Install guide: a Package managers table with each one's status (Homebrew available; winget and Omarchy in review; AUR ready, not published yet; apt and dnf repositories built, live once their signing key exists). Asked for by @NicTanghe (#149).
  • Big brushes on dense meshes keep a shorter queue of pending dabs when each dab is slow (about 150 ms of work, at least one dab, instead of always four): a big Clay stroke on a dense scan lags less and settles sooner after pen-up, with the same stroke; small brushes are unchanged.
  • Site: the README links to GitHub Releases and the guide on GitHub for networks that block sculptforge.app; sculptforge.app/security.txt (RFC 9116) points to GitHub private vulnerability reporting.
Fixed
  • Dynamic topology: after strokes in several places (zooming in between them makes many more triangles), the view could draw a long spike out of the mesh and a patch of dark, broken or missing faces until the next Undo or a full redraw. When the renderer's buffers for the remeshed areas grew, the areas drawn before kept their vertices but lost their triangles, which then drew whatever the new buffer held. The mesh itself was never damaged. Thanks @editordenis4-collab (#153).
Security
  • New local listener, the Maya Live link: per-user socket / pipe only, opt-in with a warning each time, pairing code, mesh data only (SECURITY.md).
