gh-islandmed-sculptforge.title: SculptForge v0.11.10
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.summary: Added Benchmark takes (sculptforge --benchmark-script take.sfui [project]): a UI test script's strokes, orbits, keys and waits played in real time (wall-clock pacing, 240 Hz stroke samples) in the interactive loop, with the benchmark HUD, the benchmark video…
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Added
  • Benchmark takes (sculptforge --benchmark-script take.sfui [project]): a UI test script's strokes, orbits, keys and waits played in real time (wall-clock pacing, 240 Hz stroke samples) in the interactive loop, with the benchmark HUD, the benchmark video path and a per-frame CSV (frame ms, stroke lag) beside it. Steps a take can't play in real time (shots, expectations) are skipped; steps that run commands or read other files are refused. docs/benchmark.md.
  • Insert sets (Parts > Append > Insert on the model): a model file with several objects (.obj, .glb) or a folder of .obj / .ply / .glb files becomes a set to insert from, one item at a time, with a thumbnail picker; [ and ] step to the previous / next item while inserting. Symmetry, undo and the up axis work as with one mesh. Commands insert_mesh set=<path> index=<n> and insert_set_items set=<path>. Asked by a viewer on askNK's video.
  • Sculpt the Part under the cursor (Alt+Q in every input style, the same key as Blender's; Preferences > Hotkeys changes it; in the command palette): the visible Part under the pointer becomes the active one, without moving the camera; each Part keeps its mask. The status bar says "Sculpting: ", or that no Part is under the cursor. Asked for by @ziel9627 on Discord.
  • Units (Edit > Preferences > Interface, #148, thanks @Swar55): sizes show in mm, cm, m or inches: the brush size, the active Part's width x height x depth under its name in Tool, and the size exports write in File > Import / Export. OBJ/PLY in reads the numbers in OBJ and PLY files (which have no units) as mm, cm, m (the default) or inches; open, open_obj and part_append take unit= for scripts, and STL files may be read as inches too.
Changed
  • OBJ and PLY exported from an STL are now the right size: 1000x bigger than in 0.11.9. 0.11.9 read the STL in millimetres but wrote OBJ and PLY in metres, so a 50 mm part came out as 0.05 (#148, thanks @Swar55). A scene opened from an STL, OBJ or PLY now writes OBJ and PLY in that file's own unit, an STL opened in another unit is written back in it, and decimal sizes come back exactly (12.7 mm stays 12.7, not 12.700001). Projects remember the unit. If you scaled these exports by 1000 in another app, you no longer need to.
  • USD stages in centimetres now open at their true size: 100x smaller than in 0.11.9. 0.11.9 ignored metersPerUnit, so a stage from Maya or Houdini (metersPerUnit = 0.01) opened 100x too large: a 180 cm figure was 180 m. It is now 1.8 m (#148, thanks @NicTanghe). Stages in metres, and USD files SculptForge wrote, open as before.
  • Frames overlap the CPU and the GPU: the processor builds the next frame while the graphics card draws the last, at most one frame ahead, so the input lag doesn't grow. Reading each frame's GPU time used to wait for the whole frame on some drivers (Mesa on Apple silicon), which made CPU and GPU take turns. Floor tier, a 28M-triangle scan: orbit 56 to 90 fps; a 200M-triangle scene: orbit 84 to 186 fps, big-brush strokes 51 to 191 fps.
Fixed
  • Translations: about 430 labels showed in English in Spanish, Traditional and Simplified Chinese, most visibly the whole Generate 3D panel in zh-CN; they now go through the translator in every language. The i18n test now fails on any label that skips it (only product names may), so this can't come back unnoticed.
  • Micro levels: fewer spiky shards from Clay (and the other plane brushes: Clay Block, Flatten, Trim) where a stroke's dabs pile up over rough, folded surface such as strands meeting skin, also on the symmetric side. A big brush's dab that would fold the base mesh over now sculpts the detail instead, and the detail's own plane brushes no longer push points they can't bring to the plane. Clay over rough, leaning strands can still leave small steps; a fuller fix is coming.
  • Vertex paint ignored the brush alpha: Drag Stamp, Slide Stamp, Dots and Spray painted a soft round blob with any alpha (texture painting already followed it). The paint dab now samples the alpha on the view plane, turned as sculpt dabs turn it, and reaches into the stamp's corners (#152, thanks @fxrtst).
  • Adding a paint layer on a dense top subdivision level (4M+ triangles) could leave the model drawn at its coarse preview level at rest, looking like level 1, through level changes and project reloads until a restart (#151, thanks @fxrtst). The GPU time used to decide whether full detail fits a still frame no longer counts the CPU work of the frame that added the layer, and one slow frame can no longer tip it.
  • The bottom shelf's Add a brush button draws its + exactly in the middle of the circle at every UI scale and on Retina screens; it was a font glyph that sat off centre (#150, thanks @tristratos).
  • SpaceMouse beside a pen (Discord, @fenixpoints, the first report from a real SpaceMouse): while the cap is pushed, the pointer motion and wheel a SpaceMouse driver sends for programs it doesn't know (3DxWare's defaults) no longer move the cursor off the pen or zoom toward it; with Hold during strokes off, a Move, Snake Hook or KelvinGrab drag no longer pulls the grabbed part across the view when the view turns under a still pen; gizmo, selection and stamp drags hold the view whatever the setting. Guide: Navigation > SpaceMouse troubleshooting.

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.summary: Added Line Gradient (Color, #99, requested by @Devon0209): a screen-space colour ramp for vertex paint and textures, its ends adjustable before you keep it (Enter; Esc takes it back); respects the mask, one undo step. Script: paint_gradient. Part folders (#96,…
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Added
  • Line Gradient (Color, #99, requested by @Devon0209): a screen-space colour ramp for vertex paint and textures, its ends adjustable before you keep it (Enter; Esc takes it back); respects the mask, one undo step. Script: paint_gradient.
  • Part folders (#96, thanks @ebarranco): folders in the Parts list; drag Parts in and out, fold, rename, hide and show, and move a whole folder with the gizmo's new Folder option. Saved in projects; older versions open them without folders.
  • Hyper3D Rodin (direct) in Generate 3D and the image_to_3d / text_to_3d commands (service=hyper3d, model= a Gen-2.5 tier): Hyper3D's own API with your key (system keychain only; no environment variable, no shared or trial key). One pinned https host for the API, the key sent nowhere else; the GLB only from Hyper3D's domains, capped at 200 MB and checked before import, kept in a private temporary folder deleted after import; polling backs off to 30 s. Studios: provider id hyper3d in the policy, one audit log line per generation. Thanks to ElgoogUdiab for suggesting it (#123); re-implemented in house from Hyper3D's public API documentation.
  • Cancel for Auto UV (Tool > Texture Map), beside its progress bar.
Changed
  • The console keeps one line for a job's progress ("Auto UV: 42%") instead of one line per percent.
Fixed
  • Dense meshes over the triangle budget lost their vertex colour (paint layers included) and mask while the view moved (the coarse level 0.11.7 draws then had none) and showed them again at rest. The coarse level now carries each cell's mean colour and mask from the full mesh, updated when a paint stroke ends.
  • The input style's keys for the Size slider, the Material picker and Save Snapshot came back as the Classic defaults after a restart (Blender style: F no longer showed the Size slider, S and M opened the Size slider and the Material picker) until the style was picked again in Preferences > Input; your own rebinds were not affected (#147, thanks @Velisariy).
  • Auto UV from the console, a script or an AI tool (uv_auto) froze the app while it unwrapped: about 10 s on a 327k-triangle sculpt. It now runs on the same worker as the Auto UV button, so frames keep drawing (longest frame under 100 ms, floor tier included). The next statement on the line, the AI tool's reply and a UI test's next step wait for the UVs, so uv_auto; texture_create still works in one go. Macros keep running it in place.
  • UV Editor > Pack froze the app on UDIM grids (about 18 s for a 10 x 2 grid on the lion head on a laptop, 11 s for 4 x 3): the shape packer's search now runs several densities at once, coarse first, stops as soon as an island can't be kept whole, and keeps its quarter-resolution layout instead of packing everything again at full size. 10 x 2 on the lion: 18 s -> 0.04 s. Pack, Pack at Density and every Unwrap now run on a worker thread with a progress bar and Cancel under the view.
  • Packing could shrink some islands and lay them over their neighbours: the shape packer's quarter turns mirror an island, which the fit back onto the island couldn't follow. Islands are now only turned to their smallest box first; layouts are up to 6% denser and no longer overlap.
  • Pack's status line could report more than 100% of the space used (an island bigger than a tile is shrunk to fit one); it is now measured.

Changed
  • The app icon is an orange cube on a dark tile (a new drawing, with a small cut for 16-32 px and the macOS grid): window, taskbar, dock, .ico, .icns, Flatpak, AppImage, title bar. The bust and anvil is the brand (About, What's New, site header, social previews); the SF letters are retired. docs/brand.md says which mark goes where.
  • Library: a single click uses a brush, alpha, VDM or material. Double-click still works and applies it once. Models, projects, folders, images and splats still open with a double-click (#142, thanks @NicTanghe).
  • Maya bridge (#42, thanks @tristratos): Get automatically is on once an exchange folder is chosen; a Send to Maya button sits in the top bar while the bridge is on; the Maya shelf gets Auto (on by default), which loads what SculptForge sends by itself. Both sides check only the other side's manifest (time and size), once a second; still no ports or connections. Reinstall the shelf (install_shelf()) to get the Auto button.
  • Corner axes (Draw > Camera > Axes): positive ends are filled, lettered circles (X / Y / Z), negative ends smaller rings (their letter under the pointer); far ends are smaller and fainter and the nearest is drawn on top; a translucent disc behind them (stronger under the pointer) keeps them readable on any background. A second click on the end facing you snaps to the opposite view, a drag on the disc orbits, and the name of an exact side view shows under the axes. No brush ring over the axes. Small / Medium / Large and the UI scale still apply.
  • The monthly Discord challenge posts say when it ends: entries close on the last day of the month and the winner (most 🔥 votes, ties picked by the team) is picked on the 1st, together with next month's theme.
  • Micro levels: big brushes spend about a third less time preparing each frame's shading (a 240 px stroke on a 200 million triangle head: 11 to under 8 ms a dab on the floor tier). Each changed patch is shaded on its own; its neighbours, whose shared border rarely changes, are brought up to date when the stroke ends.
Fixed
  • The guide's Edit > Preferences paths now say where Preferences is in the Classic layout (its own palette in the palette bar), and the Classic layout's Edit palette has Preferences... too. Thanks NicTanghe (#144).
  • Reconstruct Subdiv (Tool > Geometry) on open meshes (a border, e.g. a UDIM-tiled panel) no longer reads the mesh's corners and face centres the wrong way round, which failed with "a face point joins 1 quads" or gave a wrong lower level; the lower level keeps every face's UVs across seams and UDIM tiles, and stepping back up gives back the imported UVs exactly (#145, thanks @RodTDai).
  • Drag Stamp / Slide Stamp with a pen (#146, Huion RTP-700 on Windows): the stamp went weak or vanished when the pen lifted. A tablet's last samples before the lift fall towards 0, and the stamp is pressed again at every move; it now keeps the firmest pressure of the drag (Windows Ink, Wintab and Linux alike).

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Added
  • Managed policy for studios (docs/guide/studios.md "IT deployment"): policy.json in /etc/sculptforge, /Library/Application Support/SculptForge or C:\ProgramData\SculptForge (or SF_POLICY when there is none) locks AI on or off, network features, the allowed AI providers and addresses, sign-in for AI, AI tools (MCP on or off, never controlling the window, allowed kinds of command), the update check, channel and feed. Locked settings say Managed by your studio; a broken policy fails closed. sculptforge-cli --policy shows what it manages.
  • AI audit log: every AI tool (MCP) command, refused ones too, and every Brush Lab and Generate 3D request is a JSON line (time, user, host, client, command, a summary of its settings, result) in a local file or a share the policy names, rotated by size. No artwork, keys or long text. sculptforge-cli --audit-log prints the path.
  • Studio sign-in (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Auth0, Keycloak): OpenID Connect device sign-in in the artist's browser, no local listener; tokens in the keychain, sent only to the studio's own AI gateway. Edit > Preferences > AI > Studio sign-in, or sculptforge-cli --sign-in.
  • AI provider presets in Edit > Preferences > AI > Provider (also in Brush Lab): Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp server, LiteLLM proxy (a studio gateway for Bedrock, Vertex AI and Azure OpenAI) and OpenRouter.
  • Each release carries a CycloneDX software bill of materials (SculptForge-<version>-sbom.cdx.json), covered by the signed checksums. A one-page security overview for IT reviews is in the guide.
Changed
  • An empty shelf is hidden when Customize Shelves is off, and the canvas takes its space; it returns while customizing so items can be dropped back onto it. Saved layouts with empty shelves load as before (#139, thanks ebarranco).
Security
  • AI keys (Brush Lab, Hugging Face, fal.ai, Meshy) are stored in the operating system's keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service) instead of ai.json; keys already in ai.json move there at the first start. Without a keychain (SF_KEYCHAIN=none), a key lasts for the session; environment variables still work.

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Added
  • While the S (Size) pop-up is open, the brush ring stays on the model at the point where it was opened and shows the size being set, live while dragging and before Enter while typing a number (#138). O (Falloff) draws the inner Falloff ring the same way. The ring lies under the pop-up so its number stays readable.
  • Simplified Chinese interface (Preferences > Interface > Language): the Traditional Chinese translation by yoyomaimai (#114) in simplified characters, reviewed for mainland usage (鼠标, 软件, 文件, 视图, 菜单, 设置, 工具栏, 默认 and 预设, 撤销, rows and columns), every label covered. Brush and tool names stay in English. The characters come from a small built-in Noto Sans SC subset (SIL OFL), so nothing needs installing. zh-CN, zh-SG and zh-Hans codes select it; zh-TW, zh-HK and zh-MO keep Traditional.
Changed
  • Help > Connect an AI tool is the in-app guide to live mode: 1. pick your tool (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, or any other in the list) with the exact command or settings for this install, now for the live-mode server (sculptforge-cli --mcp --attach, listed as sculptforge-live beside a headless sculptforge entry); 2. the live-mode switch; 3. what happens next; four example prompts with Copy. The plan notes moved to a Plans and sign-in tooltip; the headless server and the Claude Desktop bundle are in the user guide.
  • The live-mode dialogs (Let an AI tool control this window?, Allow this AI step?) look like the app's other dialogs: one text width, two buttons of one width (the answer first), no close box (Deny or Escape), the code in a large font instead of a scaled-up small one. While the approval is open the Connect window steps aside, so two dialogs never stack; after Approve it closes and the badge takes over.
  • Show SculptForge on Discord shows the new SF icon.
Fixed
  • Show SculptForge on Discord stays up to date. Changes made in quick succession (opening files, typing the challenge) used to be dropped by Discord after the fifth in 20 seconds. Now the latest always arrives. After Discord restarts, your status is back within seconds instead of a minute.
  • Discord no longer shows SculptForge while it isn't running. Runs by scripts and test tools (benchmarks, offscreen checks) never show it, whatever the preferences say. On Linux, a process SculptForge starts (an AI worker) can no longer keep the connection, and the status, open after SculptForge quits.
  • --measure-idle reported about 100 % of one core on Windows while the app sat idle: it timed itself with the C library's clock, which on Windows counts wall time, not processor time. It now reads the process's real CPU time on every OS. Measured from outside on Windows (RTX 3060), idle 0.11.1 and 0.11.2 (a sphere open) use 0.00 % of a core, and Linux uses 0.7 %: there was no busy loop. The idle tests now also fail if the app uses more than 2 % of a core over 30 s.
  • The Paint menu jittered on a short screen (reported at 1280x720 fullscreen, thanks ebarranco): taller than the space under the menu bar, it scrolled, its colour picker shrank under the scrollbar, the menu stopped scrolling and grew again, every frame. A menu that scrolls now widens by its scrollbar instead.

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Added
  • Live mode: an AI tool sculpts in the open window while you watch. Turn on Edit > Preferences > AI > Let AI tools control this window (off by default) and connect Claude Code or any MCP client with sculptforge-cli --mcp --attach. You approve each connection (a 6-digit code), an AI connected badge has Disconnect, every step lands in Undo labelled AI:, and files outside the project, overwrites, scripts and the network ask you first. The AI can see its work (viewport_image, view_turntable, view_set), draw strokes in screen space (stroke_screen), block out forms from Forge Spheres in one call (blockout) and check proportions (measure, scene_overview). Local only: a socket / pipe just your user can open, no network port.
Fixed
  • Shading after strokes: a data race in the GPU vertex upload (several threads writing the same vertex's cavity bits) could leave rare wrong shading after a stroke. Each vertex is now written once.

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Added
  • Help > Connect an AI tool (while AI features are on): an "I have a subscription" picker (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, other tools) and, for this install, the exact command or configuration for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity CLI, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, Cursor, VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains AI Assistant, Zed, Windsurf (Devin Local), GitHub Copilot CLI, Cline, Continue, Kiro, Amazon Q Developer CLI, Warp, Goose, opencode, Rovo Dev CLI, LM Studio, Jan and the OpenAI Agents SDK, each checked against the vendor's documentation, with Copy buttons. Remote-only apps (the ChatGPT and Grok apps, Rovo on the web) are named as such: SculptForge runs no network server.
  • A Claude Desktop bundle (SculptForge-*.mcpb) for Windows, macOS and Linux on every release, and server.json for the official MCP registry.
  • The MCP server (sculptforge-cli --mcp) gains viewport_image (a clay-shaded picture of the scene from any angle, to check each step) and recipes as MCP prompts: a creature head, a stylised bust from a reference image, a game-ready asset (retopology, UVs, bake, LODs), rock variations and a step-by-step lesson. Its server info carries a title and clearer instructions.
  • AppImage: SculptForge.AppImage --cli ... runs the command-line tool inside it (so MCP clients can start it).
  • Guide (Scripting > AI agents): every client's setup, your own agent, and plain function calling with sculptforge-cli --schema for the OpenAI, Gemini and xAI APIs.
  • Freeze Levels (subdiv_freeze, dyntopo freeze_levels=true): turning on Dynamic on a Part with subdivision levels offers to keep the level shown as one plain mesh and turn Dynamic on, one undo step, instead of a dead-end message. The Draw palette shows the same button while Dynamic waits on levels.
  • View > Views: Front, Back, Left, Right, Top and Bottom buttons (Numpad 1 / 3 / 7, Ctrl for the opposite side, in every input style), and named saved views: Save View (Ctrl+Alt+Numpad 0), click a name to go back, Numpad 0 for the last one. Saved with the project.
  • Mask darkness (Preferences > Interface and Tool > Masking).
Changed
  • The app icon is the orange SF mark (as on sculptforge.app) in the task bar, Dock, Start menu, launchers and the title bar; the bust stays as the illustration in Help > About, What's New and the membership card.
  • Masked areas show as a cool dark tint with a soft edge instead of near-black, so the form stays readable.
  • The wireframe fades edges shorter than a few pixels: a dense mesh shows a light veil, not a dark moire.
  • Options that are on (toggles) have an accent-tinted fill in every colour scheme, not just a lighter grey.
  • Quad Remesh guide curves draw smooth, with stroke smoothing while drawing and a dark outline for contrast.
  • Tool > Geometry (from Discord): Divide (keeps levels) and Subdivide (removes levels) are named for what they do and sit apart: Micro in its own Micro Detail group, Subdivide under Change the Mesh (no levels). On a Part with levels, Subdivide asks first ("This removes your N subdivision levels"), with Don't ask again; Delete Lower and Delete Higher ask too (Ctrl+Z still brings the levels back).
  • Tool > Parts > Extract says to mask first when there's no mask, instead of only greying out its buttons.
Fixed
  • Quick Remesh and Tool > Remesh > Voxel Remesh of an open Part (the Stylised Head starter, open at the neck, especially after a Move pull near the neck) gave a thin shell full of holes: the outside flowed in through the opening. Open borders are now capped before the voxels are made (only for the remesh; the Part's own surface is not touched), and a Part that still isn't a closed solid (borders that can't be capped) is left unchanged with a message pointing to Tool > Geometry > Close Holes, instead of a broken result.
  • UV Editor at UI scale 2.4 (a 4K screen): the On model: Colours / Checker row was cut off and Frame was drawn over it, so clicking Frame toggled Colours. The toolbar now measures each control (in the interface language) and wraps onto more lines when it needs to; every control is where it is drawn.

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.summary: Fixed Orbiting a dense scan with a micro level right after big strokes is smoother on slower computers: the shading that catches up after the strokes now takes a few milliseconds a frame while the view moves, and the rest when it stops (on scans of around 100…
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Fixed
  • Orbiting a dense scan with a micro level right after big strokes is smoother on slower computers: the shading that catches up after the strokes now takes a few milliseconds a frame while the view moves, and the rest when it stops (on scans of around 100 million triangles; smaller ones were already smooth).
  • Help > Benchmark no longer stops at "settling" on slower computers when the scene takes a few seconds to open.
  • Move, Scale and Rotate (the Transform gizmo and the transform command) with a sculpt layer active now record into that layer, masked or not, like a stroke (#133, thanks Devon0209): the base mesh stays, the layer's weight dials the move in and out, undo works. With Base mesh active they move the base and every layer, as before.
  • Micro levels: Sharp Crease, Crease and Pinch at high intensity left prominent random noise. They now pull the height profile together the way the brushes pull a mesh, resampling the heights from where the pull brings the surface, so nothing grows from dab to dab; big brushes stay clean too (#125, reported by RodTDai).
  • Wire on a micro level showed nothing; it now draws the edges of the level below the micro level (quad diagonals left out, as on a mesh) on the micro surface (#128, reported by RodTDai).
  • With Edit > Preferences > AI > Enable AI features off, the Mesh menu still showed a Generate 3D section; it is now From Image and holds only the offline Relief, Inflate and Stamp (the AI entries were already gone). The status messages after opening an image point there too (reported by ebarranco on Discord).
  • A pen lying still in range (laid on the tablet, or held still above it) kept sending a hair of tilt and sub-pixel motion, and each event counted as the pen in use: the mouse and trackpad could neither move the cursor nor click for as long as it lay there, and the pen pulled the cursor back to itself. With a Wacom, a SpaceMouse and a trackpad on a Mac the window seemed frozen and the mirror's X out of reach (reported by phoenix on Discord). Only touching, buttons, coming into range, pressure and real movement count now.
Added
  • Rotation for vector displacement stamps (#136, thanks DonnieAlex): with the VDM brush, Sculpt > Brush > Vector Displacement > Stamp rotation has Follow stroke direction (Drag Stamp turns with the drag; off, the drag only sizes the stamp), Angle and Angle jitter (a random turn per stamp), kept per brush like the alpha options.
  • Brush files keep the alpha's Angle and Angle jitter as well as Follow stroke direction: Save Brush Settings on a custom brush writes all three into it, so shared brushes (brush codes, .sfpack) turn their alpha the same way.
  • Maya style view keys (#134, thanks RodTDai): hold Alt, then add Ctrl, and a left drag rolls the view (left / right); Alt+F frames the active Part; Alt+H resets the view (front, upright, perspective, everything in view). Ctrl first (or both together) still masks with Ctrl+Alt, on the model and beside it.
  • Edit > Preferences > Input > Wheel zooms toward the pointer (#134): the wheel zooms toward the point of the model under the pointer, which stays put. On with the Maya style; the other styles keep zooming toward the middle (the box turns it on in any style). Reset view is also an action in the Controls window, for a key of your own.
  • Help > Record a performance trace (#127, thanks RodTDai): while on, sculptforge-trace.log beside sculptforge.log records every frame over 33 ms with where its time went (events, dabs, UI, GPU uploads, drawing, GPU time), each stroke's timings, commands that held up the frames, background jobs starting and ending, the mesh size, subdivision and micro level, and the GPU, driver and CPU. Off by default and costs nothing when off; two files of 2 MB at most (sculptforge-trace-previous.log); a local file only, nothing is sent anywhere.
  • Traditional Chinese interface (#114, translation by yoyomaimai): Preferences > Interface > Language (the button with its Chinese name; saved as zh-TW). About 740 labels, Taiwan usage, brush and tool names kept in English; anything not translated yet stays in English. The Chinese glyphs come from a small embedded subset of Noto Sans CJK TC (SIL OFL), loaded only while the interface is in Chinese.
  • The title bar's triangle count adds the micro triangles of the visible Parts while there are any ("20.5k + 5.24M micro"), and so does the classic look's ActiveTris readout (#125).
Changed
  • Micro levels: a big brush stroke on a dense scan finishes sooner after the pen lifts. The dabs still waiting at the lift go through the plain mesh's own batched path (exactly what the plain brush does), and the stroke stays one undo step.
  • UV Editor > Pack: Columns x Rows (#135, thanks RodTDai): the UDIM Tiles slider is now a Columns (1-10) and Rows (1-10) grid, so a 10 x 2 layout fills 1001-1020 and 4 x 3 stays four tiles wide. Pack at Density spills within the Columns too. Projects keep their grid; new ones take the last one used. Scripts: uv_pack and uv_unwrap take columns= and rows= (tiles= works as before).
  • New icon and logo.
  • Spanish and Traditional Chinese cover the whole interface: about 950 labels and help texts added to each (UV Editor, Quick Remesh, Preferences > Input, Packs, Bake, Fill layers, Forge Spheres, SpaceMouse...), from 47% and 44% of the interface to 100%. A new test keeps it there: a label without both translations fails the build.
  • Tool > Remesh > Voxel Remesh: the Resolution slider goes from 32 to 512 (was 64 to 400), as the remesh resolution= command does (asked by fxrtst on Discord). 512 is safe on 8 GB: a 28M-triangle scan in about 8 s (14 s on 4 cores) into about 760k triangles; a round 2M sculpt in about 3 s into about 2.5M triangles, 2.2 GB at the peak.
  • Big brushes keep up better on 6+ core machines: with a brush of 160 px or more, the lighting now follows the brush's own shape while you drag, and the exact shading lands behind it and at pen-up, so big strokes stay closer to the pen. Machines with fewer cores keep the previous behaviour.

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.title: SculptForge v0.11.1
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.summary: Added Rename and organise your Lit Spheres (#124, thanks Pumaman101): Rename... and Move to folder (existing folders, New folder...) in the right-click menu of the material picker, Render > Materials and the Library's Material tab rename or move the image in…
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Added
  • Rename and organise your Lit Spheres (#124, thanks Pumaman101): Rename... and Move to folder (existing folders, New folder...) in the right-click menu of the material picker, Render > Materials and the Library's Material tab rename or move the image in the Lit Spheres folder; a name in use is refused, nothing is overwritten, and projects that use a renamed one still find it (by its pixels). Sub-folders of the Lit Spheres folder (one level) are headings in all three lists. Pack, studio-folder and project-only Lit Spheres show the items greyed out with the reason. Scripts: rename_litsphere, move_litsphere.
  • Dropping an image onto the Library's Material tab loads it as a Lit Sphere (#124); dropped on the canvas it does what it did before.
  • Founding Members: the first 100 members keep a Founding Member badge, their name in the credits (Help > About, the website's Members page) and their price for good; the membership page counts the places left (website/founding.json).
  • One-click update (the update banner's Update button) for the Linux AppImage and the Windows installer and portable zip: background download with progress and Cancel, then Restart now or Later (installs at quit). Files come only from SculptForge's GitHub releases (every redirect checked, TLS verified); the release's SHA256SUMS.txt must carry an Ed25519 signature under the key built into the app, and the package must match its checksum, before anything is written in place or run. The AppImage is replaced in one atomic rename with the old file kept as .old until the new version has started; a new version that doesn't start is rolled back. Flatpak, .deb/.rpm, AUR and Homebrew installs are never replaced (the banner names the command or says to download). macOS keeps the Download button for now. See the guide's Installing > Updating.
  • Member builds (Preferences > Updates): GitHub sign-in with the device flow for the "SculptForge Member Builds" app, which can only read the member repository's releases; the token lives in the OS keychain (Windows Credential Manager, Secret Service on Linux; macOS later), never in settings or logs, and Sign out removes it. The update check then also lists the member releases; they are verified exactly like public ones.
  • Big-mesh tip: shown once, the first time a scene holds more than about 20 million triangles (micro levels counted): what got faster on dense meshes and the settings that matter (Background Preview, View resolution), with Performance settings and Got it. Never during a stroke, a benchmark, the welcome, What's New or the quick tour; stored in project.json as soon as it shows, so it never comes back.
  • Pen pressure per brush (#122, requested by Zoldyck-Kill): every brush has its own Pen pressure: Size and Strength switches, Use global / On / Off, in Brush > Pen pressure, Brush Lab and Edit > Preferences > Tablet. Use global follows Pressure > Size / Strength as before; On and Off override them for that brush. Kept per brush with its other settings (Save Brush Settings keeps them, Reset Brush to Default puts back the default) and in a custom brush's .sfbrush. Move, KelvinGrab, KelvinTwist, KelvinScale, Tendril and Elastic Tendril start with Size off; older saved settings load as Use global. Command: brush_pen_pressure size=on|off|global strength=on|off|global.
  • Quick Remesh (Tool > Remesh, #121, thanks Zoldyck-Kill): with it on, Shift+R, or N held while clicking or dragging on the background, remeshes the active Part at the Voxel Remesh resolution in the background (progress bar and Cancel as the button; Keep Masked and Keep Texture apply). One undo step per remesh; a stroke or undo made while it runs is never overwritten (it remeshes again). Both keys are free in every key style and change in Preferences > Hotkeys; on the model a press stays a brush stroke.
  • Remesh after each stroke (Tool > Remesh, off by default, #121): after pen-up, a stroke that stretched edges past 1.6 times their length remeshes the active Part in the background; sculpting never waits for it. Not on Parts with subdivision levels, sculpt layers or a painted texture.
  • Rodin 2.5 (Hyper3D) via fal.ai (#123, thanks ElgoogUdiab): Generate 3D > fal.ai > Model lists Rodin 2.5 and Rodin 2.5 Fast. Image and text both work; the untextured GLB goes through the usual import and remesh. Uses your fal.ai key (FAL_KEY), nothing else is contacted. Commands: image_to_3d service=fal model=fal-ai/hyper3d/rodin/v2.5, text_to_3d service=fal model=fal-ai/hyper3d/rodin/v2.5 (other fal models keep Hunyuan3D 3.1 Rapid for text).
  • Studio mode: --studio studio.json (or a studio build) starts SculptForge with no outside connections: no public update check, AI services, community gallery or Discord presence, and network sockets only on this computer. Only the studio's own update channel or mirror is reached. --offline (or SF_OFFLINE=1) does the same with nothing allowed. See the user guide's "Offline deployment".
  • Touch screens and trackpads: two fingers over the model pinch to zoom and twist to roll the view, and on a touch screen slide to pan; they never sculpt. One finger on a touch screen still sculpts. Thanks to phoenix (Discord) for the report.
  • Hold during strokes (Preferences > Input > SpaceMouse, on by default): while you sculpt, paint or mask, the SpaceMouse leaves the view alone and its buttons do nothing, so a hand on the cap never moves the model under the pen or mouse. Pointer events from a SpaceMouse that the system also lists as a mouse are ignored. Thanks to phoenix (Discord).
Changed
  • Faster builds from source: on Linux the build links with mold when it is installed and precompiles the standard library and glm headers; app code the tests also run is a static library both link, so it compiles once. Packagers: -DSCULPTFORGE_MOLD=OFF keeps the system linker (the release packages do), -DSCULPTFORGE_PCH=OFF turns the precompiled headers off. See docs/build-speed.md.
  • The command search and the Library filter also find Lit Spheres by "material capture" and "material image".
  • Membership: Member Requests (one request per member per month: brushes, alphas, materials, small tweaks; "Requested by @name" on each item; out to members at month end, free for everyone a month later) replace the monthly brush and alpha pack, on the website, in the app, the guide and the README.
  • The membership card: the full card shows on the first start only (and from Help > Support); after that a small card along the bottom of the canvas comes at a good moment (about 20 minutes of active sculpting in a session, a Save Render, the first start after an update, the monthly challenge's results), at most once a week, never mid-stroke or during a job. Become a member, Not now (a week) and I'm already a member, which signs in with GitHub like member builds: a member never sees it again (and gets member builds); no sign-in hides it for three months. Signed-in members never see it. The 10-hour reminder and the old "Maybe later" are gone.
  • Memberships: Member ($5 / month or $48 / year) and Studio ($150 / month, up to 10 artists) replace Supporter, Insider, Studio and the one-time payment, on the website, in the support card, the Quick tour, the welcome note, the update banner ("Members get betas early") and the guide.
  • Betas are a member perk: X.Y.Z-beta.N is published in the private members' repository and posted in
  • Release packages on staging: the merge batch builds the release packages on the staging branch beside CI, and main reuses them. A release batch carries the version bump, so the release promotes packages that were already built and tested for the exact tagged commit: tag to published takes about 5 minutes instead of about 25.

gh-islandmed-sculptforge.title: SculptForge v0.11.0
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.summary: Added Fast Big Brushes (Experimental) (Preferences > Performance, off by default): a dab that reaches more than 150,000 vertices takes its plane from an even sample of them and turns the shading along with the move it makes (from the brush's own slope, no…
gh-islandmed-sculptforge.html:
Added
  • Fast Big Brushes (Experimental) (Preferences > Performance, off by default): a dab that reaches more than 150,000 vertices takes its plane from an even sample of them and turns the shading along with the move it makes (from the brush's own slope, no neighbour walks), and the dabs waiting for a frame go through the vertices together in one pass, so the normals, the picking structure and the GPU copy are updated once a frame instead of once a dab. Every vertex still moves by the brush itself; the exact shading follows behind the brush and when the pen lifts. Standard, Clay, Flatten, Crease, Pinch and Sharp Crease; Trim takes the sampled plane and shading but not the fused pass. Small brushes, Smooth, Layer, Inflate, Nudge, Clay Block, alphas and masked areas are placed dab by dab as before. The result matches the dab-by-dab stroke to within about 2% of how far it moved the surface (tests/test_beta_boost.cpp).
  • Brush packs: 60 built-in brushes in six packs (Clay & Form, Hard Surface, Organic & Skin, Cloth & Folds, Damage & Wear, Ornament), made from SculptForge's own recipe engine and procedural alphas. A pack brush picked the first time brings its alpha (and turns it along the stroke where that helps). Guide chapter Brush packs.
  • Six new procedural alphas: Cobblestone, Leather Grain, Hex Plates, Knit, Bolt and Chips (21 built-in alphas in all).
  • Sort menu on the brush grid and list, the Alpha palette, the Material picker and the Library: A-Z (the default), Recent, and Pack (brushes, alphas). Saved in the preferences. The Alpha palette gets a filter field.
  • Mask by peaks, Mask by colour and Mask by facing (mask_by_peaks, mask_by_color, mask_by_facing), and brush_use name=... to pick a library or pack brush from scripts and macros.
  • Brush recipes (.sfbrush, brush codes) may name a built-in alpha and alphaFollow; older files are unchanged.
  • Quick tour (Help > Quick tour, the welcome, and once when the Classic sculpting keys are picked): ten slides with pictures of SculptForge; Show me opens and flashes the panel while the tour waits in a bar at the bottom. The last slide is about memberships; Maybe later closes it for good. Guide chapter Quick tour for experienced sculptors (replaces the old comparison chapter).
  • Experimental toggles in Preferences > Performance, all off by default. Live Move: the GPU draws a Move drag from the grab's start positions and the whole move is applied once at pen lift (one grab, equal to the per-frame grabs to 1e-6). It falls back to the normal Move with masks, hidden faces, sculpt layers, micro levels, Connected Only or View falloff (SF_LIVE_MOVE=0/1). Background Preview: the predictive preview is drawn for background dabs (meshes of 2M+ vertices), and the frame no longer waits for a batch; the solver's dabs are unchanged (SF_BG_GHOST=0/1). Fast Upload: stroke uploads are packed into persistently mapped staging buffers (GL_ARB_buffer_storage) and copied on the GPU (SF_PERSISTENT_UPLOAD=0/1). The research behind them, including a design for focus detail on billion-polygon assets, is in docs/design/perf-moonshots.md.
  • Cmd+, / Ctrl+, opens Preferences (#111, suggested by fenixpoints).
  • Show SculptForge on Discord (Preferences > Integrations, off by default; idea by ebarranco): Discord shows SculptForge, its icon and the elapsed time; optionally "Monthly challenge: " (typed, 64 characters at most) and the file's name (never its folder). Nothing else is sent. It talks only to the Discord app on the same computer through Discord's local connection (no network connection, no port, no sign-in), sends its status and nothing else, and ignores whatever Discord sends back. See the guide's "Show SculptForge on Discord".
Changed
  • Tool > Masking is one panel of buttons with pictures and a hint each: Shapes, Mask by and Adjust, with their options under Mask by options.
  • Brushes, alphas, materials and Library files list A-Z by default (alphas and materials were in a fixed order; Library projects were newest first, which is still one click away under Sort: Recent).
  • The command search (F3) finds features by plain sculpting words: remesh, voxel, retopo, quads, multires, groups, clip, trim, slice, folders, insert, kitbash, vertex color ("Quad Remesh (also: retopo)").
  • Scripts, commands and file names use SculptForge's own names throughout (part_*, forgesphere_*, bridge_*, facegroup_*, load_litsphere, library_open, layout=classic, input_style classic, the --facegroups flag, the SCULPTFORGE_LITSPHERE_PATH variable). Scripts, macros, keymaps, radial menus, packs, projects and preferences from older versions still load: their old names are read once and mapped to the new ones. The old command-line flag and environment variable names are no longer read.
  • Micro levels on slower computers: while a stroke runs, the shading of what it changed takes at most about 10 ms a frame (measured on the computer), so big strokes keep up with the pen; the rest of the shading follows right after, as before.
Removed
  • The library export plug-in for another sculpting app and opening its library files through it. A folder of numbered Bridge files still opens as one scene.
Fixed
  • Pattern brushes on micro levels (#120, reported by RodTDai): a brush recipe on a micro level was a plain Standard dab, without its surface pattern (Dragon Scales, Skin Pores, Cracks...) and building up even when the recipe carves. It now keeps the pattern and its depth's sign there; planes, pinch and drag still don't apply to micro levels.
  • Windows portable zip starts on a fresh PC (#109, reported by git-tiger): the Visual C++ runtime (msvcp140, vcruntime140, vcruntime140_1) now ships next to sculptforge.exe in the zip and the installer; before, a PC without the Visual C++ Redistributable couldn't start it. When SculptForge can't start (no OpenGL 3.3, an old graphics driver) it now says why in a message box, with the log's path, instead of quietly exiting.
  • Move with Pressure > Size on a pen (#122, reported by Zoldyck-Kill): Move and the Kelvinlet grab brushes set the area they grab at the press, when a pen barely touches, so with Pressure > Size on they grabbed only a few percent of the brush and seemed not to work. They now always grab with the full brush size; Pressure > Strength still applies.
Downloads

New here? install/ explains which file to pick, or install with one command: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/islandmed/SculptForge/main/install/install.sh | sh (macOS / Linux), irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/islandmed/SculptForge/main/install/install.ps1 | iex (Windows PowerShell). Each file is also attached without its version number (e.g. SculptForge-macos.dmg) so links to releases/latest/download/... always get the newest build.

gh-hitkeeen-blender-ai-mcp-addon.html:
mcp-for-blender-pro — v1.0.0

First public release of the AI assistant and MCP server for Blender.

Highlights

  • Visual Studio workspace: chat, scene objects, viewport snapshots, approvals and a task board
  • 21 scene tools: create, inspect, edit, capture, asset search, Blender API consult, export
  • One assistant or a team: manager, workers and reviewers for structured multi-step tasks
  • Your choice of AI: ChatGPT/GPT, Claude, Gemini, Ollama or compatible custom endpoints
  • Saved connections: keep work and personal profiles separate, multiple keys per provider
  • Built-in MCP server: connect OpenCode and other clients via authenticated Streamable HTTP
  • Multilingual interface: English, German, French, Spanish, Chinese
  • Portable Python 3.13 runtime bundled for Windows x64

Requirements

  • Blender 4.2+
  • Windows x64

Install

  1. Download blender-ai-mcp-addon-v1.0.0.zip below.
  2. In Blender: Edit > Preferences > Add-ons > Install from disk...
  3. Select the zip and enable the addon.
  4. Open the Studio workspace and add your AI connection.

Documentation and getting started guide: see the README on the main page.

gh-sollumz-sollumz.title: Sollumz v2.9.0
gh-sollumz-sollumz.summary: This release includes a complete YMAP rework, texture dictionary support, easier ways to build game asset libraries, an expanded presets system, and many bug fixes, including compatibility fixes for Blender 5.2. Highlights YMAP Rework YMAP support has been…
gh-sollumz-sollumz.html:
This release includes a complete YMAP rework, texture dictionary support, easier ways to build game asset libraries, an expanded presets system, and many bug fixes, including compatibility fixes for Blender 5.2.

Highlights

YMAP Rework

YMAP support has been rewritten from scratch, adding support for all features available in YMAPs, including: entities, MLO instances, LOD hierarchies, car generators, occluders, timecycle modifiers, LOD lights, and grass batches.

Maps are no longer represented as object hierarchies in the outliner. Everything is managed from the new Maps panel in the Sollumz Tools sidebar, with a workflow similar to the MLO workflow. Check out the documentation.

LOD Hierarchy Management

Sollumz now understands and handles LOD hierarchies in YMAPs. Related YMAPs are organized into map groups, where each container becomes a YMAP file on export. Parent/child LOD relationships are managed across the whole map group, so hierarchies spanning multiple YMAPs survive export correctly.

Partial hierarchies can still be imported, but containers with missing LOD parents or children are locked down, and editing is limited (e.g. entities cannot be deleted) to prevent data loss on export.

A new Map LOD Hierarchy viewport tool allows you to visualize and modify the hierarchy in 3D: drag and drop entities to link or unlink parents.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6943f26f-fda8-4d6f-a8d9-0ff41d225c33

Automatic Partitioning

Set a map container to Auto, and Sollumz partitions its items into the standard sub-containers for you: strm, long, critical and per-interior YMAPs. Manual layouts can be collapsed back to Auto, or Auto containers converted to manual if you want full control.

MLO Instances

MLO instances can now also be added to YMAPs. The MLO panel in the sidebar has a new "Create MLO Instance" button that creates a copy of your MLO as a single object, ready to be placed in a map.

Grass Batches

Full grass batch import/export is now supported, with geometry-nodes-based generation and preview. Each grass batch is configured through a list of "templates", which define the models that can appear and their per-model settings (e.g. scale, LOD distance). The geometry nodes modifier then uses these templates to scatter the grass instances over a base mesh.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1dc4e768-4078-4235-9225-09f5d6e3e8c4

The geometry nodes require Blender 5.0 or newer. Import/export still works on all supported versions, since the grass batch itself is just a regular mesh containing only vertices. This also means some manual editing is possible.

LOD Lights

LOD lights can now be imported and exported, and a new Bake LOD Lights operator collects the lights of all entities in a map group and generates the lodlights/distlodlights YMAPs automatically, categorized by size, partitioned, and with streaming extents computed for you.

Texture Dictionary Support

YTDs can now be imported and exported. A new Texture Dictionaries panel lets you create dictionaries and add or remove textures manually, or add source mesh objects that automatically gather all images used by their Sollumz shaders, with a per-image toggle to control what gets included.

HD texture dictionaries (+hi) can also be managed from this panel. On export, textures marked as HD are exported to a +hi.ytd at full resolution, while the base .ytd contains half-resolution versions. This also works with embedded textures on drawables, fragments, and drawable dictionaries: when HD textures are present, a +hidr.ytd/+hifr.ytd/+hidd.ytd is exported alongside the main asset.

Asset Libraries

The new Build Asset Library operator scans a directory of game files and builds .blend asset libraries from the YTYPs and assets it finds, including files inside RPFs. If a YTYP contains an MLO, the whole MLO is also saved as an asset, which can later be placed in maps as an MLO instance.

The operator parallelizes the work across multiple Blender background processes, significantly speeding up the build. Libraries are managed from the add-on preferences and integrate with Blender's asset browser.

When entities are instanced from YMAPs or YTYP MLOs, archetypes are resolved from these libraries, after first checking the current .blend. Assets built by Sollumz also embed metadata, allowing features like LOD light baking and entity LOD distance resolution to work without loading the original game files.

Presets Everywhere

The presets system has been extended, and presets are now available in far more places: collision flags and materials, lights, shaders, fragment bone physics, archetypes, entities, extensions, MLO rooms, portals, timecycle modifiers, car generators, and grass templates/batches. Presets apply to all selected items at once where applicable.

The updated system stores JSON files instead of XML files. They can be found at %APPDATA%\Blender Foundation\Blender\X.Y\config\sollumz\presets. Existing XML presets are migrated automatically on first load.

gh-sollumz-sollumz.title: Sollumz v2.8.0
gh-sollumz-sollumz.summary: This release is a big step forward for Sollumz. Thanks to our collaboration with Rockstar Games and Cfx.re on their new Materia library, Sollumz now supports native binary formats import and export. This means you can now work with Legacy (Gen8) and Enhanced…
gh-sollumz-sollumz.html:
This release is a big step forward for Sollumz. Thanks to our collaboration with Rockstar Games and Cfx.re on their new Materia library, Sollumz now supports native binary formats import and export. This means you can now work with Legacy (Gen8) and Enhanced (Gen9) binary assets directly, making the workflow smoother and more straightforward.

Check out their official announcement.

Blender 5.0 should now be fully compatible as well. This was a major update, so if you run into any issues, please let us know and report them. Sollumz continues to support Blender versions 4.0 through 4.5 too.

Highlights

Binary Formats Import/Export

A long-requested feature is finally here: direct import and export of GTAV’s native binary resource formats without requiring intermediate XML conversions. With this update, you can now work directly with .ybn, .ydr. .ydd, .yft, .yld and .ytyp files. This includes full support Legacy and Enhanced assets.

When exporting, you can choose which formats and game versions to target. For example, during development you can just export for the version you primarily work with, e.g. Legacy, then for release and final testing export to both Legacy and Enhanced simultaneously from the same .blend file. CodeWalker XML support is still and will remain available for those workflows that require it.

Import/Export

All this is powered by PyMateria, the Python bindings for the new Materia library by Cfx.re. Upon installation of Sollumz, you will be prompted to install the new dependencies. PyMateria is an optional dependency and currently only available on Windows. If you are on a different platform, you won't be able to access the new functionality provided by PyMateria but Sollumz will continue working as it did before.

For Developers

Developers interested on trying PyMateria can install it with: 

pip install --index-url https://static.cfx.re/whl/ pymateria
Important: before using PyMateria, please make sure to read and understand the PyMateria License Agreement.

We also have a new library, szio. Independent from Blender, provides an unified interface for working with game files in any format, binary or CW XML. This is what Sollumz now uses for its import and export functionality. Can be installed with: 

pip install szio

Automatic Vehicle Windows Shattermap Generation

Creating shattermaps for vehicle windows has always been a tedious process. This update introduces automatic shattermap generation on export, with the same quality as the shattermaps found on vanilla vehicles. Note that this requires PyMateria to be installed.

To use this functionality, make sure you setup your vehicle models correctly:

  • Set window meshes to use VEHICLE VEHGLASS shader.
  • Set the associated collisions to use one of the CAR GLASS materials. CAR GLASS BULLETPROOF will make it undestructible.
  • On the mesh, the blue channel of color attribute Color 1 allows you to define the exposed edges of the window (those without a frame around them). These edges will break cleanly without leaving a border of broken glass.

The old workflow with manual shattermaps is still available so your existing projects will work as they did before, but we recommend switching to the automatic generation. If you want to keep the manual shattermaps when importing a vehicle, you can enable the new import setting Import Window Shattermaps.

This example shows the new Preview Windows button which lets you inspect the generated shattermaps. This allows you to verify that your vehicle windows are setup correctly without going in-game.

Preview Windows Shattermaps

Vertex Paint Tools

This release also brings new tools available in vertex paint mode. You can find them in the new "Vertex Paint" side panel.

  • Isolate Channel. View and paint specific color channels, including the alpha channel.
  • Multi-Object Vertex Paint. Paint multiple objects at the same time.
  • Transfer Channels. Copy channels between color attributes.
  • Palette Picker. Used along with tint shaders, works like a color picker that sets the correct brush color for the column you select from a palette texture in an Image Editor.
  • Gradient. Paints a gradient between two points.
  • Terrain Painter. The old Terrain Painter panel has been moved here.

Isolate & Multi-Object

Gradient

Palette Picker

Most of these functions are also available through a new vertex paint pie menu. The default keybind is Shift+T.

Name Tables

Sollumz can now load name tables and will attempt to resolve hashed names when importing assets. With proper name tables (shared by the community or your own), this will reduce the amount of hash_1234ABCD names you find after importing assets. This is particularly important when importing binary drawable dictionary .ydd files.

You can configure which name table files to load under Preferences > General. Simply add your .txt or .nametable files to the list:

gh-sollumz-sollumz.html:
Highlights

Cloth Support

Import and export of cloth simulation assets is now supported. This includes cloth embedded in vehicle and prop fragments (YFT) as well as character cloth (YLD).

For character cloth, the YLD file is automatically imported or exported together with the corresponding ped drawable dictionary (YDD) file.

A new 'Cloth Tools' panel provides various utilities to configure and visualize cloth-specific attributes and diagnose potential setup issues.

Multi-Selection Support in Archetypes/MLO UI

The item lists in the Archetypes and MLO UI panels now support multi-selection. When multiple items are selected, changes to properties will apply to all selected items simultaneously. Properties that cannot be edited across multiple items will be shown as disabled (greyed out).

Multi-selection follows standard list controls:

  • Shift + Click: Extends the selection range.
  • Ctrl + Click: Toggles selection of individual items.

Additionally, new buttons have been added next to the lists to select all items with a single click, taking into account the current filter.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/925a5532-0f25-4943-97cd-eb5248f8681a

Improved Vehicle Shader Preview

You can now preview vehicle shaders more accurately within Blender, including dirt level, paint colors, and lighting (on/off states).

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94055772-b5b2-4890-b571-b5d8e04daa57

gh-sollumz-sollumz.html:
Highlights

Support Sollumz Development

Sollumz is made possible through the dedication of its developers and the support of its community. If you have found Sollumz useful for your projects and want to support its continued development of new features and improvements, please consider contributing.

You can support the development by donating through:

  • Open Collective
  • GitHub Sponsors

All supporters will receive a special role and gain access to an exclusive channel on our Discord.

Damaged Model Support

Fragments with damaged models can now be imported and exported. These fragments contain an additional drawable and bound composite that replace the main model when entering "damaged" state.

Favorites System for Shaders & Collision Materials

You can now mark specific entries in the shaders and collision materials lists as favorites. A new filter toggle lets you easily view only your favorites.

Changing Material Shader

Now, you can change the shader of a material while preserving its parameters and without the need to create a new material.

gh-sollumz-sollumz.html:
Highlights

Blender 4.2 & Extensions Repository

Added support for Blender 4.2 and now Sollumz can be installed as an extension from our repository https://repo.sollumz.org/.

  • First, add https://repo.sollumz.org/ as a remote repository by navigating to Preferences > Get Extensions > Repositories > + > Add Remote Repository:

  • Next, search for "Sollumz". You will see two available versions to install:

  1. Sollumz: The official release version, identical to what you can download from this page.
  2. Sollumz (Development): The latest development build, which may be unstable. Use this version to test new features and updates, and provide feedback to help us improve.
  • Once installed, you can easily update to newer versions directly within Blender whenever they are released.
Cable Meshes Support

Meshes using the cable shader can now be imported and exported. These are simplified meshes containing only vertices and edges, with no faces. Each vertex includes several user-editable attributes, such as cable radius and micromovements scale. To modify cable meshes, explore the new Cable Tools panel located under Sollumz Tools > Drawables.

Shared Textures Directories

The new Shared Textures preference lets you specify additional directories to search for textures during model import. If a texture isn't found in the model's texture directory, these directories will be searched for a match.

gh-sollumz-sollumz.summary: Highlights Versioning System Sollumz 2.4 introduces a new data versioning system that aims to make Sollumz backward compatible with .blend files saved on older Sollumz versions, reducing obstacles when wanting to update Sollumz but still having unfinished…
gh-sollumz-sollumz.html:
Highlights

Versioning System

Sollumz 2.4 introduces a new data versioning system that aims to make Sollumz backward compatible with .blend files saved on older Sollumz versions, reducing obstacles when wanting to update Sollumz but still having unfinished projects. As a result, projects created with Sollumz 2.3 or 2.3.1 are compatible with 2.4.

When opening .blend files saved with an old Sollumz version for the first time on a newer version, an automatic upgrade process occurs that changes old Sollumz data to be compatible with the current Sollumz version.

Capsule Light Gizmo

Capsule lights now have a gizmo that shows the capsule bounds, providing visual feedback closer to how the light would appear in-game.

Capsule lights can now also be resized in the 3D view via a cage gizmo that appears when hovering the active capsule light, similar to how built-in light gizmos work.

capsule_light.webm

Light Culling Plane Gizmo

Lights with culling plane enabled will now show a gizmo representing the culling plane. This gizmo is a round plane with a cross pattern and arrows to indicate in which side of the culling plane the light is visible. It can be interacted with to move the culling plane along its normal (change its offset).

To change the culling plane normal, there is a new workspace tool “Edit Light Culling Planes” that will show a rotation widget to modify the normal on the selected light. The tool UI also has buttons to flip the plane or set its normal to the XYZ axes.

culling_plane.webm

Typed Shader Parameters

Shader value parameters are now aware of their data type and the UI will display an appropriate widget instead of always four values. For example: from one up to four values, a color picker for RGB and RGBA parameters or a checkbox for boolean parameters. This removes a lot of useless values from the UI, reducing the visual clutter in the panel. In addition, the “Array Parameters” panel has been merged with the “Value Parameters” panel.

gh-sollumz-sollumz.summary: Changelog Features Reworked the animation support: (#709, #758) Support import/export of all animation tracks. Support import/export of clip tags and properties. Improved UV animation tooling. Now supports different transformations, not only translation. Added…
gh-sollumz-sollumz.html:
Changelog

Features
  • Reworked the animation support: (#709, #758)
    • Support import/export of all animation tracks.
    • Support import/export of clip tags and properties.
    • Improved UV animation tooling. Now supports different transformations, not only translation.
    • Added sprite sheet UV animation tool.
    • Support camera animations.
    • Support assigning a target per animation, instead of selecting a single skeleton on import. Useful if a clip dictionary contains animations for different skeletons or other targets.
    • Various fixes for issues present in the old system.
  • Added support for fragment breakable glass. (#745)
  • Implemented Sollumz shader for distance_map shader. (#710)
Fixes
  • Export drawables with strict shader parameter order to prevent OpenIV crashes. (#702) [@Kc2693]
  • Fixed emissive_clip and other emissive shaders. (#688, #707) [@ook3D]
  • Fixed errors when Blender language is not English. (#708, #716)
  • Fixed incorrect parsing of boolean XML values. (#714, #718)
  • Fixed joints exported with wrong bone tag when manually set. (#726) [@Hancapo]
  • Fixed instancing and rotation errors in YMAP import. (#704. #725, #728)
  • Fixed “Apply Bone Flags” not working for all selected bones. (#731) [@Hancapo]
  • Fixed auto-create archetype including physicsDictionary for YFTs. (#740) [@Hancapo]
  • Fixed bound spheres growing on export. (#729)
  • Fixed Very High lods under physics children drawables not being exported. (#727)
  • Fixed import errors with hashed shader filenames. (#671)
  • Fixed shattermaps rotation on rotated bones. (#739)
  • Fixed collision parenting breaking on export. (#746)
  • Fixed drawable objects not created in same collection as converted meshes. (#744)
  • Fixed MLO archetype export. (#706)
  • Fixed auto-calculated bone tags. Now it is a per-bone setting, instead of an export setting. (#751)
  • Fixed “Generate Wheel Instances” tool. Now supports more than 4 wheels (middle wheel bones) and different wheel meshes for front and middle/rear wheels. (#756)
  • Fixed “Successfully exported 'file.xml'” message showing when no files were exported. (#749)
Other Changes
  • Added new archetype flags. (#722) [@Hancapo]
  • Improved “Object Location & Rotation” tools. (#757) [@ook3D]

[!WARNING]
Do not update Sollumz mid-project, it can cause compatibility issues and/or data loss.
